title.zh: 卷二十六 列傳第七 王敬則 陳顯達
title.en: Volume 26 Biographies 7: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda
title.raw: 卷二十六 列傳第七 王敬則 陳顯達 Volume 26 Biographies 7: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda

sentences.zh: 王敬則 陳顯達

translations.literal: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda

sentences.zh: 王敬則，晉陵南沙人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze was a native of Nan'sha in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze was a man of Nan'sha in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 母為女巫，生敬則而胞衣紫色，謂人曰：「此兒有鼓角相。

translations.literal: His mother was a shamaness; when she bore Jingze the afterbirth was purple, and she told people: 「This boy has the countenance of drums and horns.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a shamaness; when Jingze was born the afterbirth was purple, and she said to those about her: 「This child bears the mark of drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 」敬則年長，兩腋下生乳各長數寸。

translations.literal: 」When Jingze grew up, a nipple several inches long grew under each armpit.
translations.idiomatic: 」As he grew, a nipple several inches long sprouted under each armpit.

sentences.zh: 夢騎五色師子。

translations.literal: He dreamed of riding a five-colored lion.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed he rode a lion of five colors.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，善拍張。

translations.literal: In his twenties he was skilled at the hand-drum.
translations.idiomatic: By his twenties he was master of the hand-drum.

sentences.zh: 補刀戟左右。

translations.literal: He was appointed to the left and right of the sabers and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted among the saber-and-halberd guards.

sentences.zh: 景和使敬則跳刀，高與白虎幢等，如此五六，接無不中。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era the emperor had Jingze perform leaping blade; the height matched the White Tiger banner standard, and so five or six times—every catch true.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jinghe he was made to dance the leaping blade to the height of the White Tiger standard; five or six passes in a row, and not one miss.

sentences.zh: 補俠轂隊主，領細鎧左右。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief of the Valiant Cavalry company and led the fine-mail attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was named chief of the valiant cavalry company and led attendants in fine mail.

sentences.zh: 與壽寂之同斃景和。

translations.literal: Together with Shou Jizhi he killed Emperor Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shou Jizhi together killed Emperor Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，以為直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Jingze was made Colonel of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, Jingze was made colonel of the direct gate.

sentences.zh: 坐捉刀入殿啟事，系尚方十餘日，乃復直閤。

translations.literal: For drawing a blade to enter the hall and report affairs he was held at the Imperial Workshop for more than ten days, then restored to the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He had once drawn a blade to enter the hall on business and was held at the imperial workshop for ten-odd days before returning to the direct gate post.

sentences.zh: 除奮武將軍，封重安縣子，邑三百五十戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Exerts Martial Might and enfeoffed as Viscount of Chong'an with a fief of three hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who exerts martial might and made viscount of Chong'an, fief of three hundred fifty households.

sentences.zh: 敬則少時于草中射獵，有虫如烏豆集其身，擿去乃脫，其處皆流血。

translations.literal: When Jingze was young he hunted in the grass; insects like black beans clustered on his body, and only when he picked them off did they come away—every spot bled.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he hunted in the tall grass; insects like black beans swarmed on him, and only when he picked them off did they leave—each place wept blood.

sentences.zh: 敬則惡之，詣道士卜，道士曰：「不須憂，此封侯之瑞也。

translations.literal: Jingze loathed this and went to a Daoist for divination; the Daoist said: 「Do not grieve—this is an omen of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The sight revolted him; he sought out a Daoist, who said: 「Have no fear—this is an omen of enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 」敬則聞之喜，故出都自效，至是如言。

translations.literal: 」Jingze heard it with joy, and so left the capital to prove himself; now it came to pass as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze took heart, left the capital to win merit, and now saw the words fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，以敬則為龍驤將軍、軍主，隨寧朔將軍劉懷珍征壽春。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was made General of the Flying Dragon and army commander, following the Pacifying North general Liu Huaizhen in the campaign against Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he was named general of the flying dragon and army commander and marched with Liu Huaizhen, general of pacifying the north, against Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 殷琰遣將劉從築四壘於死虎，懷珍遣敬則以千人繞後，直出橫塘，賊衆驚退。

translations.literal: Yin Yan sent his general Liu Cong to build four forts at Dead Tiger; Huaizhen sent Jingze with a thousand men to circle behind, strike straight out of Hengtang, and the rebel host fell back in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yan sent Liu Cong to raise four forts at Dead Tiger; Huaizhen sent Jingze with a thousand men around the rear, straight through Hengtang, and the rebels broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，出補曁陽令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant at Court and went out to serve as magistrate of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant at court and sent out as magistrate of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 敬則初出都，至陸主山下，宗侶十餘船同發，敬則船獨不進，乃令弟入水推之，見一烏漆棺。

translations.literal: When Jingze had first left the capital, he reached below Mount Luzhu; more than ten clan boats set out together, but Jingze's alone would not advance, so he had his younger brother go into the water to push—and they saw a lacquered coffin.
translations.idiomatic: On his first departure from the capital he came to Mount Luzhu; a dozen clan boats cast off together, but his would not move until his brother went into the water to push—and there lay a lacquered coffin.

sentences.zh: 敬則曰：「爾非凡器。

translations.literal: Jingze said: 「You are no common vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze said: 「You are no common thing.

sentences.zh: 若是吉善，使船速進。

translations.literal: If this is auspicious, let the boat hurry on.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean us well, let the boat fly forward.

sentences.zh: 吾富貴，當改葬爾。

translations.literal: When I am rich and noble, I shall give you a new burial.
translations.idiomatic: Should I rise, I will bury you again in honor.

sentences.zh: 」船須臾去。

translations.literal: 」In a moment the boat went on.
translations.idiomatic: 」At once the boat surged ahead.

sentences.zh: 敬則旣入縣，收此棺葬之。

translations.literal: Once Jingze had entered the county seat, he took up this coffin and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the county seat he retrieved the coffin and buried it properly.

sentences.zh: 軍荒之後，縣有一部劫逃紫山中為民患，敬則遣人致意劫帥，可悉出首，當相申論。

translations.literal: After the armies had scourged the land, a band of brigands fled into Mount Zi and plagued the people; Jingze sent men with word to their chief that if they all came forward he would hear them out.
translations.idiomatic: When the wars had laid the district waste, one band of robbers hid on Mount Zi and preyed on the people; Jingze sent word to their chief that if they surrendered together he would treat with them fairly.

sentences.zh: 治下廟神甚酷烈，百姓信之，敬則引神為誓，必不相負。

translations.literal: The shrine god below his rule was fierce, and the people trusted it; Jingze called the god to witness that he would not betray them.
translations.idiomatic: A local temple god was feared as harsh, and the people believed in it; Jingze swore before the god that he would not break faith.

sentences.zh: 劫帥旣出，敬則于廟中設會，於座收縛，曰：「吾先啟神，若負誓，還神十牛。

translations.literal: Once the brigand chief had come out, Jingze held a feast in the shrine and seized and bound them at the seats, saying: 「I have already told the god that if I break my oath, I owe the god ten oxen.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief came in, Jingze gave a feast in the shrine and had his men seize the band at table, saying: 「I told the god already—if I break my vow, I owe ten oxen.

sentences.zh: 今不違誓。

translations.literal: Today I do not break the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Today I keep my word.

sentences.zh: 」卽殺十牛解神，幷斬諸劫，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: 」He at once killed ten oxen to release the god, and beheaded all the brigands besides; the people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: 」He slaughtered ten oxen for the god, beheaded every brigand, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Outside Section Member.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to outside section member.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，隨太祖拒桂陽賊於新亭，敬則與羽林監陳顯達、寧朔將軍高道慶乘舸<舟習>於江中迎戰，大破賊水軍，焚其舟艦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, following the Grand Ancestor to resist the Guiyang rebels at Xinting, Jingze with the Feathered Forest inspector Chen Xianda and the Pacifying North general Gao Daoqing rode light boats (received ge; note boat-xi) on the river to meet battle, smashed the rebel fleet, and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui year two he followed the Grand Ancestor against the Guiyang rebels at Xinting; Jingze, Chen Xianda of the feathered forest, and Gao Daoqing, general of pacifying the north, took light craft on the river to meet the fight, routed the rebel navy, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 事寧，帶南泰山太守，右俠轂主，轉越騎校尉，安成王車騎參軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he bore the title of Administrator of South Taishan, chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry, then was shifted to Commandant of the Yue Cavalry and staff officer on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-horse staff.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he held south Taishan as administrator, led the right valiant cavalry, then became commandant of the Yue cavalry and an aide on the Prince of Ancheng's staff.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王狂虐，左右不自保，敬則以太祖有威名，歸誠奉事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cangwu was savage and cruel; those about him could not keep themselves safe. Jingze, seeing that the Grand Ancestor had a commanding name, turned his loyalty and served him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cangwu was violent and cruel, and his attendants lived in fear. Jingze saw the Grand Ancestor's weight in the realm and gave him his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 每下直，輒往領府。

translations.literal: Every time he came off duty he went at once to the command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he left the palace watch he went straight to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 夜著青衣，扶匐道路，為太祖聽察蒼梧去來。

translations.literal: At night he put on blue clothes, crept along the roads on hands and knees, and listened for Cangwu's comings and goings on the Grand Ancestor's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: By night he wore plain blue, crawled the streets, and spied out Cangwu's movements for the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖命敬則於殿內伺機，未有定日。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor ordered Jingze to watch inside the hall for a chance to strike, but no day was yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor told Jingze to wait inside the hall for the moment to act, though no day was set.

sentences.zh: 旣而楊玉夫等危急殞帝，敬則時在家，玉夫將首投敬則，敬則馳詣太祖。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Yufu and the others, pressed hard, killed the emperor; Jingze was at home at the time, and Yufu was about to cast the head to Jingze—Jingze galloped to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Yufu and his fellows, driven to extremity, slew the emperor; Jingze was at home when Yufu meant to throw him the head—Jingze rode at once to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮蒼梧所誑，不開門。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor feared a trick from Cangwu and would not open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor feared a ruse from Cangwu and kept the gate shut.

sentences.zh: 敬則於門外大呼曰：「是敬則耳。

translations.literal: Jingze shouted outside the gate: 「It is Jingze!
translations.idiomatic: Jingze cried at the gate: 「It is Jingze!

sentences.zh: 」門猶不開。

translations.literal: 」Still the gate did not open.
translations.idiomatic: 」The gate stayed closed.

sentences.zh: 乃於牆上投進其首，太祖索水洗視，視竟，乃戎服出。

translations.literal: He then cast the head over the wall; the Grand Ancestor asked for water, washed it, and looked—only then did he don armor and come out.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled the head over the wall; the Grand Ancestor called for water, washed it, and looked—then at last he armed and came out.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，進敬則號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt rose, Jingze was advanced to General of the Champions.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Jingze was promoted to general of the champions.

sentences.zh: 太祖入守朝堂，袁粲起兵夕，領軍劉韞、直閤將軍卜伯興等於宮內相應，戒嚴將發。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor entered to hold the audience hall; on the night Yuan Can raised troops, the commander Liu Yun, Colonel of the Direct Gate Bu Boxing, and others were to answer from within the palace—the guard was drawn up and they were about to move.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor went in to hold the audience hall; on the night Yuan Can rose, Liu Yun the commander, Bu Boxing of the direct gate, and others were to answer from inside the palace—the guard was called and they were ready to strike.

sentences.zh: 敬則開關掩襲，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Jingze opened the pass and struck by surprise; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze threw open the gate and fell on them by surprise; every one was cut down.

sentences.zh: 殿內竊發盡平，敬則之力也。

translations.literal: The secret rising inside the hall was wholly put down—Jingze's doing.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden rising in the hall was crushed to the last man—Jingze's work.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard, Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to general of the right guard, regular attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 增封為二千五百戶，尋又加五百戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased to two thousand five hundred households; soon another five hundred were added.
translations.idiomatic: His fief rose to two thousand five hundred households, and before long five hundred more were added.

sentences.zh: 又封敬則子元遷為東鄉侯，邑三百七十戶。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqian was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxiang with a fief of three hundred seventy households.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanqian was enfeoffed as marquis of Dongxiang, fief of three hundred seventy households.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，為中領軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he was made Colonel of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi court was founded, he was made colonel of the central army.

sentences.zh: 太祖將受禪，材官薦易太極殿柱，從帝欲避土，不肯出宮遜位。

translations.literal: When the Founder was about to receive the abdication, master carpenters urged replacing the pillars of the Hall of Supreme Pole; the abdicating emperor wished to avoid earth and would not leave the palace to yield the throne.
translations.idiomatic: As the Founder prepared to take the mandate, carpenters proposed new pillars for the Hall of Supreme Pole. The abdicating emperor, seeking to dodge the omen of earth, refused to quit the palace and yield.

sentences.zh: 明日，當臨軒，帝又逃宮內。

translations.literal: The next day, when he was to appear at the audience hall, the emperor fled back within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he was due at the audience hall, the emperor bolted back into the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 敬則將轝入迎帝，啟譬令出。

translations.literal: Jingze led a carriage in to welcome the emperor and urged him at length to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze drove a carriage in to fetch the emperor and pleaded with him until he came out.

sentences.zh: 帝拍敬則手曰：「必無過慮，當餉輔國十萬錢。」

translations.literal: The emperor clapped Jingze's hand and said: 「Surely there is no need for such worry; I will reward the Assistant State with one hundred thousand cash.」
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Jingze's hand and said: 「You fret too much. I shall give the Assistant State a hundred thousand cash.」

sentences.zh: 建元元年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、平北將軍、南兖州刺史，封尋陽郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, overseer of military affairs in the five provinces Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Yan; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xunyang commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1 he was sent out with the staff, as regular attendant of the scattered riders, overseer of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and governor of Southern Yan, and enfeoffed Duke of Xunyang with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 加敬則妻懷氏爵為尋陽國夫人。

translations.literal: Jingze's wife, née Huai, was further ennobled as Lady of the Xunyang state.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's wife, of the Huai clan, was raised to Lady of the Xunyang state.

sentences.zh: 二年，進號安北將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 虜寇淮、泗，敬則恐，委鎮還都，百姓皆驚散奔走，上以其功臣，不問，以為都官尚書、撫軍。

translations.literal: When the northerners raided the Huai and Si, Jingze in fear abandoned his post and returned to the capital; the people all fled in panic. Because he was an old merit-holder, the throne did not punish him and made him Minister of State Offices and Pacifier of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy struck the Huai and Si, Jingze in fear left his command and fled to the capital; the countryside broke and ran. As a founding servant he went unscathed and was named minister of state offices and pacifier of the army.

sentences.zh: 尋遷使持節、散騎常侍、安東將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, General Who Pacifies the East, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon shifted to bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered riders, General Who Pacifies the East, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 郡舊多剽掠，有十數歲小兒於路取遺物，殺之以徇，自此道不拾遺，郡無劫盜。

translations.literal: The commandery had long been rife with robbery; when boys of ten-some years picked up lost things on the road he had them killed as a warning, and from then on none picked up what others dropped and the commandery knew no brigands.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery had long plagued the commandery. He executed boys of ten or so who picked up lost goods on the road as a public warning; thereafter no one touched what was not his, and brigandage ceased.

sentences.zh: 又錄得一偷，召其親屬於前鞭之，令偷身長掃街路，久之乃令偷舉舊偷自代，諸偷恐為其所識，皆逃走，境內以清。

translations.literal: He also seized a thief, summoned his kin before him and had them flogged, and ordered the head thief to sweep the streets at length; only then did he make the head thief denounce old thieves to replace him. The rest, fearing recognition, all fled, and the region was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He caught another thief, had his family flogged before him, and set the ringleader to sweep the streets for a long while before forcing him to name his fellows. The gang, afraid of being identified, scattered, and the district grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 出行，從市過，見屠肉栟，嘆曰：「吳興昔無此栟，是我少時在此所作也。」

translations.literal: On an outing he passed through the market, saw a butcher's meat frame, and sighed: 「Wuxing never had such a frame in the old days—it is one I made here in my youth.」
translations.idiomatic: Passing the market on tour he saw a butcher's rack and sighed: 「Wuxing never had these in the old days. I built that one as a young man here.」

sentences.zh: 遷護軍將軍，常侍如故，以家為府。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Protects the Army, his regular attendant post unchanged, and used his own house as headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Protects the Army, still regular attendant, and kept his household as his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 三年，以改葬去職，詔贈敬則母尋陽公國太夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year he left office for a reburial; an edict ennobled Jingze's mother as Grand Lady of the Xunyang ducal state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he resigned to rebury the dead; the throne ennobled his mother Grand Lady of the Xunyang ducal state.

sentences.zh: 改授侍中、撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Palace Attendant and Pacifier of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned palace attendant and pacifier of the army.

sentences.zh: 太祖遺詔敬則以本官領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: The Founder's testamentary edict had Jingze in his existing office also hold the post of Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In his death edict the Founder left Jingze in his present rank and added magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 尋遷為使持節、散騎常侍、都督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡軍事、鎮東將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, overseer of military affairs in Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia five commanderies, General Who Guards the East, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff, regular attendant of the scattered riders, overseer of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General Who Guards the East, and administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was granted one set of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2 he was given one suite of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 會土邊帶湖海，民丁無士庶皆保塘役，敬則以功力有餘，悉評斂為錢，送臺庫以為便宜，上許之。

translations.literal: The lands of Kuaiji border lakes and sea; commoners, noble and base alike, all kept embankment duty. Jingze, finding labor to spare, assessed it all as cash and sent it to the central treasury as a convenience measure; the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji lies along lakes and sea, and every household, gentle or common, owed embankment labor. Jingze, seeing surplus effort, levied it all in coin and forwarded it to the central treasury as a savings to the state. The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良啟曰：

translations.literal: Prince Zi Liang of Jingling memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zi Liang of Jingling wrote:

sentences.zh: 伏尋三吳內地，國之關輔，百度所資。

translations.literal: I reflect that the inner lands of the Three Wu are the state's strategic belt, the source of every revenue.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the Three Wu heartland is the realm's hinge, the wellspring of every levy.

sentences.zh: 民庶凋流，日有困殆，蠶農罕獲，飢寒尤甚，富者稍增其饒，貧者轉鍾其弊，可為痛心，難以辭盡。

translations.literal: The people waste away day by day toward ruin; silkworms and fields seldom yield; hunger and cold are worst of all. The rich grow richer, the poor sink deeper into want—heartbreaking beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: The people drift toward ruin; silk and grain rarely prosper; hunger and cold are worst. The wealthy grow fatter while the poor bear a heavier yoke—grievous beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 頃錢貴物賤，殆欲兼倍，凡在觸類，莫不如茲。

translations.literal: Of late cash has grown dear and goods cheap, nearly to double; whatever one touches is alike.
translations.idiomatic: Lately money has grown scarce and goods cheap, nearly twofold; the same wound runs through every trade.

sentences.zh: 稼穡難劬，斛直數十，機杼勤苦，匹裁三百。

translations.literal: Fieldwork is bitter toil yet a bushel fetches only tens; the loom is weary labor yet a bolt brings only three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers toil bitterly yet a bushel sells for tens; weavers labor hard yet a bolt earns only three hundred.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，實亦有由。

translations.literal: The reasons for this truly have their roots.
translations.idiomatic: There are real causes for this.

sentences.zh: 年常歲調，旣有定期，僮恤所上，咸是見直。

translations.literal: The annual levy already has fixed seasons; what corvée and relief payments submit are all at current value.
translations.idiomatic: Yearly taxes fall on fixed dates, and every corvée and relief payment is reckoned at present rates.

sentences.zh: 東間錢多剪鑿，鮮復完者，公家所受，必須員大，以兩代一，困於所貿，鞭捶質系，益致無聊。

translations.literal: In the east coins are mostly clipped and filed, few whole; what the government accepts must be full weight, counting two for one. Trapped in what they must buy, men are flogged and pawned until life is unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern coin is mostly clipped and filed, rarely whole, yet the state demands full weight and takes two for one. Beaten and pawned to meet the exchange, people are driven past endurance.

sentences.zh: 臣昔忝會稽，粗閒物俗，塘丁所上，本不入官。

translations.literal: I once served in Kuaiji and roughly knew local ways: what embankment laborers paid in never entered government coffers.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in Kuaiji I learned the local ways: embankment dues never entered the treasury.

sentences.zh: 良由陂湖宜壅，橋路須通，均夫訂直，民自為用。

translations.literal: It was because dikes and lakes must be banked and bridges and roads kept open—labor was equalized, rates set, and the people used it for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes and lakes had to be raised, bridges and roads kept clear; labor was shared, rates fixed, and the people spent it on their own needs.

sentences.zh: 若甲分毀壞，則年一脩改；

translations.literal: If section A was ruined, it was repaired once a year;
translations.idiomatic: If one stretch failed, it was mended once a year;

sentences.zh: 若乙限堅完，則終歲無役。

translations.literal: if section B stood firm, there was no corvée all year.
translations.idiomatic: if another stood sound, no labor was levied that year.

sentences.zh: 今郡通課此直，悉以還臺，租賦之外，更生一調。

translations.literal: Now the commandery levies this cash throughout and sends it all to the capital; beyond rent and tax there is yet another exaction.
translations.idiomatic: Now the commandery taxes this sum everywhere and sends it all to the capital, so beyond rent and land tax the people pay yet again.

sentences.zh: 致令塘路崩蕪，湖源泄散，害民損政，實此為劇。

translations.literal: Hence dikes and roads collapse, lake sources drain away—harm to the people and hurt to government, and this is the worst of it.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes and roads fall in ruin and lakeheads run dry—harm to the people and damage to rule, and this levy is the chief cause.

sentences.zh: 建元初，狡虜遊魂，軍用殷廣。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan the crafty foe still roamed; military costs were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyuan the northern foe still haunted the borders and military costs swelled.

sentences.zh: 浙東五郡，丁稅一千，乃有質賣妻兒，以充此限，道路愁窮，不可聞見。

translations.literal: In the five eastern commanderies of Zhe the household tax was one thousand; some even pawned wives and children to meet it. The misery on the roads is unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhedong's five commanderies the household tax ran to a thousand; families pawned wives and children to pay. The wretchedness along the roads is more than one can bear to tell.

sentences.zh: 所逋尚多，收上事絕，臣登具啟聞，卽蒙蠲原。

translations.literal: Arrears were still many and collection had stalled; I memorialized in full and at once received remission.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears remained heavy and collection had stopped; I laid the facts before the throne and was granted remission at once.

sentences.zh: 而此年租課，三分逋一，明知徒足擾民，實自弊國。

translations.literal: Yet this year's rent still shows one third in arrears. I know well that this only harries the people and in truth weakens the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this year's rent is still one third unpaid. It plainly harasses the people and in truth enfeebles the realm.

sentences.zh: 愚謂塘丁一條，宜還復舊，在所逋郵卹，優量原除。

translations.literal: I hold that the embankment-labor rule should return to the old way, and that local arrears should be reviewed and generously forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that embankment labor be restored to the old rule and local arrears reviewed and generously remitted.

sentences.zh: 凡應受錢，不限大小，仍令在所，折市布帛。

translations.literal: Whatever cash is due, great or small, should still be taken in the locality and exchanged for cloth on the market.
translations.idiomatic: All cash payments, large or small, should be collected locally and swapped for market cloth.

sentences.zh: 若民有雜物，是軍國所須者，聽隨價准直，不必一應送錢。

translations.literal: If the people have sundry goods needed by army and state, let them be accepted at fair price and there is no need to demand coin in every case.
translations.idiomatic: If households hold goods the army and state require, let them be taken at fair value; coin need not be demanded every time.

sentences.zh: 于公不虧其用，在私實荷其渥。

translations.literal: The public purse loses nothing of its use, while in private men truly feel the grace.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury loses nothing it needs, and in private life the people feel real relief.

sentences.zh: 昔晉氏初遷，江左草創，絹布所直，十倍於今，賦調多少，因時增減。

translations.literal: When the Jin first crossed south and the east was newly founded, silk and cloth were worth ten times today's price; how much was levied rose and fell with the times.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first crossed the river and the southeast was new, silk and cloth cost ten times what they do now; tax quotas shifted with the age.

sentences.zh: 永初中，官布一匹，直錢一千，而民間所輸，聽為九百。

translations.literal: In the early Yongchu era official cloth was one bolt for one thousand cash, yet what the people paid was allowed at nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchu a bolt of official cloth was reckoned at a thousand cash, yet private payment was accepted at nine hundred.

sentences.zh: 漸及元嘉，物價轉賤，私貨則束直六千，官受則匹准五百，所以每欲優民，必為降落。

translations.literal: By the Yuanjia era prices fell further: in private trade a bundle fetched six thousand, yet the government counted a bolt at five hundred—so whenever the throne wished to favor the people, it lowered the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuanjia goods had cheapened again: private bundles sold for six thousand while the state valued a bolt at five hundred—each time the court meant to ease the people, it cut the quota.

sentences.zh: 今入官好布，匹堪百餘，其四民所送，猶依舊制。

translations.literal: Today fine cloth sent to government is worth little more than a hundred per bolt, yet what the four classes deliver still follows the old rule.
translations.idiomatic: Today good cloth taken by the state is worth barely a hundred a bolt, yet the people still pay under the old scale.

sentences.zh: 昔為刻上，今為刻下，氓庶空儉，豈不由之！

translations.literal: Once the squeeze came from above; now it comes from below—the common folk are emptied. Is this not why?
translations.idiomatic: Once the state scraped them from above; now it scrapes them from below—the people are bled dry. What else could hollow them out?

sentences.zh: 救民拯弊，莫過減賦。

translations.literal: To save the people and lift their distress, nothing surpasses cutting levies.
translations.idiomatic: To rescue the people and lift their distress, nothing surpasses lighter taxes.

sentences.zh: 時和歲稔，尚爾虛乏，儻值水旱，寧可熟念。

translations.literal: In years of peace and plenty they are still empty; should flood or drought come, how can one bear to think of it?
translations.idiomatic: Even in peaceful, fertile years they are destitute; if flood or drought should come, the thought is unbearable.

sentences.zh: 且西京熾強，實基三輔，東都全固，實賴三河，歷代所同，古今一揆。

translations.literal: Moreover, the western capital grew mighty on the three auxiliaries, and the eastern capital stood firm on the three rivers—the same through every dynasty, the same rule in every age.
translations.idiomatic: The western capital grew strong on the three auxiliaries; the eastern capital held fast on the three rivers—alike in every dynasty, one measure for all time.

sentences.zh: 石頭以外，裁足自供府州，方山以東，深關朝廷根本。

translations.literal: Beyond Shitou there is barely enough to supply prefectures and provinces; east of Fangshan lies what deeply secures the court's root.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shitou the land barely feeds the prefectures; east of Fangshan lies the deep root of the throne.

sentences.zh: 夫股肱要重，不可不卹。

translations.literal: The limbs of the realm are vital; they must not go uncared for.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern provinces are the arms and legs of the state—they cannot be left to wither.

sentences.zh: 宜蒙寬政，少加優養。

translations.literal: They ought to receive lenient policy and a measure of gentle nurture.
translations.idiomatic: They deserve mild governance and a little deliberate relief.

sentences.zh: 略其目前小利，取其長久大益，無患民貲不殷，國材不阜也。

translations.literal: Set aside immediate petty gain and take the lasting great profit; then there is no fear that the people's wealth will not flourish or the state's resources not abound.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice the small profit before your eyes for the large benefit down the years, and you need not fear that the people will not grow rich or the treasury full.

sentences.zh: 宗臣重寄，咸云利國，竊如愚管，未見可安。

translations.literal: Senior ministers bearing heavy trust all say this profits the state; in my humble view I do not see how it can be secure.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers entrusted with weighty affairs all call it good for the realm; by my poor lights I see no safety in it.

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 三年，進號征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his title rose to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 宋廣州刺史王翼之子妾路氏，剛暴，數殺婢，翼之子法明告敬則，敬則付山陰獄殺之。

translations.literal: The concubine Lady Lu of Wang Yi, Inspector of Guangzhou under Song, was fierce and cruel and repeatedly killed maidservants. Yi's son Faming reported this to Jingze; Jingze handed her to the Shanyin jail and had her put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu, concubine of Wang Yi—Guangzhou inspector under Song—was savage and had killed servant girls again and again. Yi's son Faming appealed to Jingze, who sent her to the Shanyin prison and had her executed.

sentences.zh: 路氏家訴，為有司所奏，山陰令劉岱坐棄市刑。

translations.literal: The Lu family petitioned; the authorities memorialized against him, and the magistrate of Shanyin, Liu Dai, was sentenced to death in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu kin brought suit; the responsible offices reported the matter, and Liu Dai, magistrate of Shanyin, was condemned to public execution.

sentences.zh: 敬則入朝，上謂敬則曰：「人命至重，是誰下意殺之？

translations.literal: When Jingze came to court the emperor said to him: 「Human life is the weightiest of things—who gave the order to kill her?
translations.idiomatic: Jingze appeared at court. The emperor said to him: 「A human life is the gravest matter under heaven—who set his mind on taking hers?

sentences.zh: 都不啟聞！

translations.literal: You never reported it at all!
translations.idiomatic: And you never breathed a word of it to me!

sentences.zh: 」敬則曰：「是臣愚意。

translations.literal: 」Jingze said: 「It was this minister's own foolish notion.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze said: 「That was my own witless idea.

sentences.zh: 臣知何物科法，見背後有節，便言應得殺人。

translations.literal: I know nothing of what the statutes say; I saw that there was justification behind it and said she ought to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: I know nothing of the code in such cases; I saw cause behind the deed and judged that she deserved death.

sentences.zh: 」劉岱亦引罪，上乃赦之。

translations.literal: 」Liu Dai also took guilt upon himself, and the emperor then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Liu Dai confessed guilt as well, and in the end the emperor spared them both.

sentences.zh: 敬則免官，以公領郡。

translations.literal: Jingze was removed from office but continued to govern the commandery in his ducal capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze was stripped of his post yet still held the commandery under his noble rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍中、中軍將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 尋與王儉俱卽本號開府儀同三司，儉旣固讓，敬則亦不卽受。

translations.literal: Soon he and Wang Jian were both given their existing titles together with Open Pacification, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes; Jian firmly declined, and Jingze likewise did not accept at once.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he and Wang Jian were both offered Open Pacification, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, on their present ranks. Jian refused outright; Jingze too held back from accepting.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事、征西大將軍、豫州刺史，開府如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of the military affairs of Xiyang in Ying Province and Runan in Si Province, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu—with his open headquarters unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went out bearing the staff as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, overall commander of Xiyang in Ying and Runan in Si, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu, his grand headquarters unchanged.

sentences.zh: 進號驃騎。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷司空，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was moved to Minister of Works, his attendant post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Minister of Works, still holding his attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，遺詔改加侍中。

translations.literal: When Shizu died, the testamentary edict added Attendant-in-Ordinary to his titles.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's death the deathbed edict added Attendant-in-Ordinary to his honors.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，密有廢立意，隆昌元年，出敬則為使持節、都督會稽東陽臨海永嘉新安五郡軍事、會稽太守，本官如故，海陵王立，進位太尉。

translations.literal: Gaozong held the regency and secretly harbored a design to depose the throne. In the first year of Longchang, Jingze was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, commander of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an, and Administrator of Kuaiji, his other offices unchanged. When the Prince of Hailing was enthroned, Jingze was advanced to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong governed as regent and quietly nursed a plan to unseat the ruler. In Longchang 1, Jingze was posted out with the staff as commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, and Xin'an and as Administrator of Kuaiji, his other ranks as before. When the Prince of Hailing took the throne, Jingze was promoted to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 敬則名位雖達，不以富貴自遇，危拱傍遑，略不嚐坐，接士庶皆吳語，而殷勤周悉。

translations.literal: Though Jingze's name and rank had risen high, he did not treat himself as wealthy; he stood bowed and restless and scarcely sat down. With gentry and commoners alike he spoke only the Wu tongue, yet he was earnest and thorough in every courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: For all his fame and height of office, Jingze did not live as a rich man: he stood with folded hands, uneasy on his feet, and rarely took a seat. Gentry and common folk alike he addressed in the Wu dialect, yet his attentions were warm and exacting to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 初為散騎使虜，於北館種楊柳，後員外郎虞長耀北使還，敬則問：「我昔種楊柳樹，今若大小？

translations.literal: When he had first served as a Cavalier Attendant envoy to the northern court, he planted a willow at the northern lodge. Later the Staff Officer Yu Changyao returned from a northern mission, and Jingze asked: 「The willow I planted in those days—how large is it now?
translations.idiomatic: In his first embassy north as Cavalier Attendant he had planted a willow at the northern guesthouse. Years later Yu Changyao came back from the north, and Jingze asked him: 「That willow I set in the ground—how tall has it grown?

sentences.zh: 」長耀曰：「虜中以為甘棠。

translations.literal: 」Changyao said: 「Among the northerners they treat it as a sweet-pear memorial tree.
translations.idiomatic: 」Changyao said: 「On the northern side they honor it like the Duke of Shao's beloved tree.

sentences.zh: 」敬則笑而不答。

translations.literal: 」Jingze smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 世祖御座賦詩，敬則執紙曰：「臣幾落此奴度內。

translations.literal: When Shizu sat at the throne composing verse, Jingze held up the paper and said: 「I nearly fell within this fellow's measure.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Shizu composed poetry at the throne, Jingze took the sheet and said: 「I came within a hair of this slave's compass.

sentences.zh: 」世祖問：「此何言？

translations.literal: 」Shizu asked: 「What words are these?
translations.idiomatic: 」Shizu asked: 「What do you mean by that?

sentences.zh: 」敬則曰：「臣若知書，不過作尚書都令史耳，那得今日？

translations.literal: 」Jingze said: 「Had I been a man of learning, I would have been no more than a chief clerk in the Secretariat—how could I have reached today?
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze said: 「If I had been a scholar, I would have ended a chief clerk in the Secretariat at best—never the place I hold now.

sentences.zh: 」敬則雖不大識書，而性甚警黠，臨州郡，令省事讀辭，下教判決，皆不失理。

translations.literal: 」Though Jingze was not greatly versed in books, his nature was very sharp and quick. When he governed provinces and commanderies he had clerks read memorials aloud, issued orders and judgments himself, and never missed the right of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze was no great reader, yet his wit was keen. In the provinces he had aides read petitions aloud, then drafted his own orders and verdicts—and none of them strayed from reason.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，進大司馬，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, Jingze was advanced to Grand Marshal and his fief increased by a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingdi's accession he was made Grand Marshal and his fief grew by a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 臺使拜授日，雨大洪注，敬則文武皆失色，一客在傍曰：「公由來如此，昔拜丹陽吳興時亦然。

translations.literal: On the day the court envoy came to invest him, rain poured in torrents; Jingze's civil and military staff all turned pale. A guest at his side said: 「My lord has always been thus—even when you received Danyang and Wuxing it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The day the imperial messenger arrived to invest him, the skies opened in a flood; Jingze's civil and military officers lost color. A guest beside him said: 「You have always been like this, my lord—it was the same when you took Danyang and Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 」敬則大悅，曰：「我宿命應得雨。

translations.literal: 」Jingze was greatly pleased and said: 「My fate was meant to bring rain.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze was delighted and said: 「Rain is written into my destiny.

sentences.zh: 」乃列羽儀，備朝服，道引出聽事拜受，意猶不自得，吐舌久之，至事竟。

translations.literal: 」He then arrayed his honor guard, put on full court dress, and with drums and pipes led the procession out to the hall of audience to receive the appointment—yet he still felt ill at ease, sticking out his tongue a long while until the rite was finished.
translations.idiomatic: 」He lined up his guard of honor, donned full court robes, and with music marched out to the audience hall to take the seal—yet he could not settle his mind, his tongue lolling for a long while before the ceremony ended.

sentences.zh: 帝旣多殺害，敬則自以高、武舊臣，心懷憂恐。

translations.literal: The emperor had already killed many men; Jingze, as an old servant of the Gao and Wu houses, bore worry and fear in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already shed much blood; Jingze, a veteran of the Gao and Wu reigns, lived in growing dread.

sentences.zh: 帝雖外厚其禮，而內相疑備，數訪問敬則飲食體干堪宜，聞其衰老，且以居內地，故得少安。

translations.literal: Though the emperor outwardly heaped courtesy upon him, inwardly he was suspicious and on guard, repeatedly inquiring whether Jingze's eating and physical strength were sound. When he heard that Jingze was aging, and because he held an interior post, Jingze was able to rest somewhat easier.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the throne showered him with honor; inwardly it watched and doubted him, sending again and again to ask whether his meals and his body still held firm. Word that he was growing old, and that he sat in the inner provinces, let him breathe a little easier for a time.

sentences.zh: 三年中，遣蕭坦之將齋仗五百人，行武進陵。

translations.literal: In the third year the court sent Xiao Tanzhi leading five hundred ceremonial guards to proceed to the Wujin mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xiao Tanzhi was dispatched with five hundred ritual guards on a progress to the Wujin imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 敬則諸子在都，憂怖無計。

translations.literal: Jingze's sons were in the capital, terrified and without a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's sons in the capital were stricken with fear and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 上知之，遣敬則世子仲雄入東安慰之。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and sent Jingze's heir Zhongxiong east to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of their panic he sent Jingze's eldest son Zhongxiong east to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 仲雄善彈琴，當時新絕。

translations.literal: Zhongxiong was skilled at the zither and without peer in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong played the zither with a gift none could match in his generation.

sentences.zh: 江左有蔡邕焦尾琴，在主衣庫，上敕五日一給仲雄。

translations.literal: In the lands south of the Yangtze there was Cai Yong's scorched-tail zither, kept in the imperial wardrobe treasury; the emperor ordered that it be lent to Zhongxiong every five days.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river lay Cai Yong's famous scorched-tail zither, housed in the wardrobe treasury; the emperor commanded that it be given to Zhongxiong every fifth day.

sentences.zh: 仲雄於御前鼓琴作《懊儂曲歌》曰：「常嘆負情儂，郎今果行許！

translations.literal: Before the throne Zhongxiong struck the strings and sang the 「Regretful Nong」: 「I have long sighed that you were faithless—husband, you have truly gone so far!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong played before the emperor and sang the 「Song of Regretful Nong」: 「So long I mourned your broken faith—and now, my lord, you go through with it indeed!

sentences.zh: 」帝愈猜愧。

translations.literal: 」The emperor grew all the more suspicious and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor's suspicion and shame only deepened.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，帝疾，屢經危殆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor fell ill and repeatedly hovered near death.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 the emperor sickened and more than once stood at the edge of death.

sentences.zh: 以張瑰為平東將軍、吳郡太守，置兵佐，密防敬則。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui was made General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wu, with military aides set in place to guard Jingze in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui was named General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wu, with troops and staff assigned to watch Jingze covertly.

sentences.zh: 內外傳言當有異處分。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court, rumor said that some extraordinary measure was coming.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike whispered that some drastic step was at hand.

sentences.zh: 敬則聞之，竊曰：「東今有誰？

translations.literal: When Jingze heard it he muttered: 「Who is there in the east now?
translations.idiomatic: Jingze heard the talk and said under his breath: 「Who in the east is left to fear?

sentences.zh: 秖是欲平我耳！

translations.literal: They only mean to bring me down!
translations.idiomatic: They mean to finish me—that is all!

sentences.zh: 」諸子怖懼，第五子幼隆遣正員將軍徐嶽密以情告徐州行事謝朓為計，若同者，當往報敬則。

translations.literal: 」His sons were terrified. His fifth son, Youlong, sent the regular general Xu Yue in secret to tell Xie Tiao, acting officer of Xu Province, the whole story and ask his counsel; if Tiao agreed, he was to report back to Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: 」His sons were beside themselves with fear. The fifth, Youlong, sent the regular general Xu Yue in secret to Xie Tiao, who was administering Xu Province, to lay bare the plot and seek his word; if Tiao sided with them, he would carry word back to Jingze.

sentences.zh: 朓執嶽馳啟之。

translations.literal: Tiao seized Yue and galloped to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao seized Yue and raced to the capital with a full disclosure.

sentences.zh: 敬則城局參軍徐庶家在京口，其子密以報庶，庶以告敬則五官王公林。

translations.literal: Jingze's garrison staff officer Xu Shu had family in Jingkou; Shu's son secretly reported to Shu, and Shu told Jingze's Five-Offices aide Wang Gonglin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shu, a staff officer on Jingze's city bureau, had kin in Jingkou; Shu's son sent word to him in secret, and Shu told Jingze's Five-Offices aide Wang Gonglin.

sentences.zh: 公林，敬則族子，常所委信。

translations.literal: Gonglin was Jingze's clansman, whom he always trusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin was Jingze's kinsman, a man he had long trusted with his affairs.

sentences.zh: 公林勸敬則急送啟賜兒死，單舟星夜還都。

translations.literal: Gonglin urged Jingze to send an urgent memorial asking that his sons be granted death, and to return to the capital alone in a single boat by starlight through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin pressed him to rush a memorial begging the throne to execute his sons, then row back alone by night in a single boat.

sentences.zh: 敬則令司馬張思祖草啟，旣而曰：「若爾，諸郎在都，要應有信，且忍一夕。

translations.literal: Jingze had his Chief of Staff Zhang Sinzu draft the memorial, then said: 「If so, the young lords in the capital would surely get word—bear with it one night.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze had his chief of staff Zhang Sinzu draft the memorial, then said, 「If I did that, word would reach my sons in the capital—let it wait one night.

sentences.zh: 」其夜，呼僚佐文武樗蒲賭錢，謂衆曰：「卿諸人慾令我作何計？

translations.literal: 」That night he summoned his civil and military aides to gamble at cockalorum for stakes, and said to the gathering: 「You all want me to do what plan?
translations.idiomatic: 」That night he called his civil and military staff to gamble at cockalorum for cash and asked the room, 「What plan do you want from me?

sentences.zh: 」莫敢先答。

translations.literal: 」No one dared answer first.
translations.idiomatic: 」No one dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 防閤丁興懷曰：「官只應作耳。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Ding Xinghuai said: 「My lord ought simply to act.
translations.idiomatic: Chamberlain Ding Xinghuai said, 「My lord should simply rise.

sentences.zh: 」敬則不作聲。

translations.literal: 」Jingze made no sound.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze said nothing.

sentences.zh: 明旦，召山陰令王詢、臺侍御史鍾離祖願，敬則橫刀跂坐，問詢等「發丁可得幾人？

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned Shanyin Magistrate Wang Xun and Court Attendant Censor Zhongli Zuyuan. Jingze sat with his sword across his knees, legs sprawled, and asked Xun and the others: 「How many men could you mobilize from the corvée?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he summoned Shanyin magistrate Wang Xun and court attendant censor Zhongli Zuyuan. Jingze sat sword across his knees, legs sprawled, and asked them, 「How many corvée men can you raise?

sentences.zh: 傳庫見有幾錢物？

translations.literal: How much money and goods are in the transit storehouse?
translations.idiomatic: How much coin and goods sit in the transit storehouse?

sentences.zh: 」詢答「縣丁卒不可上」。

translations.literal: 」Xun answered: 「The county conscripts cannot be brought up.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xun said, 「The county levies cannot be mustered.

sentences.zh: 祖願稱「傳物多未輸入」。

translations.literal: Zuyuan said: 「Much of the stored goods has not yet been turned in.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyuan said, 「Most of what is stored has not yet been delivered in.

sentences.zh: 敬則怒，將出斬之。

translations.literal: 」Jingze grew angry and was about to have them taken out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze flew into a rage and was about to have them dragged out and killed.

sentences.zh: 王公林又諫敬則曰：「官是事皆可悔，惟此事不可悔！

translations.literal: Wang Gonglin again remonstrated with Jingze: 「My lord, any matter may yet be regretted and reversed—only this cannot be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gonglin pleaded again: 「My lord, anything may still be undone—only this cannot be undone!

sentences.zh: 官詎不更思！

translations.literal: Will my lord not reconsider!
translations.idiomatic: Will my lord not think again!

sentences.zh: 」敬則唾其面曰：「小子！

translations.literal: 」Jingze spat in his face and said: 「Boy!
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze spat in his face and cried, 「Pup!

sentences.zh: 我作事，何關汝小子！

translations.literal: When I act, what has it to do with you, stripling!
translations.idiomatic: When I move, what is that to you, whelp!

sentences.zh: 」乃起兵。

translations.literal: 」He thereupon raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: 」Then he took up arms.

sentences.zh: 上詔曰：「謝朓啟事騰徐嶽列如右。

translations.literal: The emperor's edict said: 「Xie Tiao's memorial exposing Xu Yue is set forth on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict read: 「Xie Tiao's memorial exposing Xu Yue is set forth at right.

sentences.zh: 王敬則稟質凶猾，本謝人綱。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze's nature is vicious and slippery; he was originally a bondsman of the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze is vicious and slippery by nature; he began as a bondsman of the Xie house.

sentences.zh: 直以宋季多艱，頗有膂力之用，驅獎所至，遂升榮顯。

translations.literal: Only because the late Song years were full of hardship did his physical strength prove useful; wherever rewards and coercion were applied, he rose to glory and prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the late Song years were hard did his brute strength find use; driven and rewarded wherever he went, he climbed to glory.

sentences.zh: 皇運肇基，預聞末議，功非匡國，賞實震主。

translations.literal: When the imperial fortune was first founded, he took part in the final counsels; his merit did not stabilize the realm, yet his rewards truly overshadowed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first founded he had a hand in the last counsels; his merit did not steady the state, yet his rewards outshone the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 爵冠執圭，身登衣袞，固以《風雅》作刺，縉紳側目。

translations.literal: His title wore the jade tablet, his person wore court robes of state; surely the Book of Odes would take him for satire—the gentry looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: He bore a noble's tablet and wore the court robes of state; the Book of Odes might have written him as a warning—the gentry watched him sidelong.

sentences.zh: 而溪谷易盈，鴟梟難改，猜心內駭，丑辭外布。

translations.literal: Yet ravines and valleys fill easily; owl and kite are hard to change—suspicion beat within, ugly words spread without.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ravines fill fast and the owl and kite do not mend; suspicion gnawed within, foul rumor ran without.

sentences.zh: 永明之朝，履霜有漸，隆昌之世，堅冰將著，從容附會，朕有力焉。

translations.literal: In the Yongming reign frost's advance was gradual; in the Longchang era firm ice was about to form—yet he went along and made his peace; I had my part in that.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongming, frost crept in by degrees; under Longchang, hard ice was forming—yet he eased along and made his peace, and I had my share in it.

sentences.zh: 及景歷惟新，推誠盡禮，中使相望，軒冕成陰。

translations.literal: When Jingli brought renewal, I treated him with utmost sincerity and ceremony; inner messengers came in unbroken files, his carriages and caps cast shade.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingli renewed the reign, I met him with open heart and full rite; palace envoys followed one on another until his coaches and caps made a shade.

sentences.zh: 乃嫌跡愈興，禍圖茲構，收合亡命，結黨聚群，外候邊警，內伺國隙。

translations.literal: Yet his suspicious traces grew, his plot for disaster took shape; he gathered runaways, knit factions and crowds, watched for border alarms without, watched for cracks in the state within.
translations.idiomatic: Then his suspicious tracks deepened and his plot for ruin took shape; he gathered fugitives, knotted factions, watched the frontiers for alarm and the state for a crack.

sentences.zh: 元遷兄弟，中萃淵藪，奸契潛通，將謀竊發。

translations.literal: Yuanyuan and his brothers were the deep pool at the center; secret wicked compacts passed through them; he was about to steal a rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyuan and his brothers were the deep pool at the center; treasonous ties ran through them in secret; he was on the verge of a stolen rising.

sentences.zh: 朓卽姻家，嶽又邑子，取據匪他，昭然以信。

translations.literal: Tiao is his marriage kin, Yue a fellow townsman—the grounds are none other, clear and to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao is kin by marriage, Yue a man of his home town—the proof is no other, plain and to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 方、邵之美未聞，韓、彭之釁已積。

translations.literal: One has not heard of Fang and Shao's beauties, yet Han and Peng's guilt is already piled high.
translations.idiomatic: We have not heard of Fang and Shao's loyalty, yet Han and Peng's guilt is already heaped high.

sentences.zh: 此而可容，孰寄刑典！

translations.literal: If this may be tolerated, upon whom shall we place the criminal code!
translations.idiomatic: If this may stand, upon whom shall the law rest!

sentences.zh: 便可卽遣收掩，肅明國憲。

translations.literal: Let him at once be seized and covered—make the national statutes severe and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be seized at once and the national statutes made sharp and clear.

sentences.zh: 大辟所加，其父子而已；

translations.literal: Capital punishment applies only to father and sons;
translations.idiomatic: Death by the highest law falls on father and sons alone;

sentences.zh: 凡諸詿誤，一從蕩滌。

translations.literal: all incidental entanglements shall be washed away in one sweep.
translations.idiomatic: all who were drawn in by mistake shall be cleared in one sweep.

sentences.zh: 」收敬則子員外郎世雄、記室參軍季哲、太子洗馬幼隆、太子舍人少安等，於宅殺之。

translations.literal: 」They arrested Jingze's sons—Gentleman-in-Attendance Shixiong, Staff Officer Jizhe, Household Groom Youlong, Crown Prince's Attendant Shao'an, and others—and killed them at their residences.
translations.idiomatic: 」They seized Jingze's sons—gentleman-in-attendance Shixiong, staff officer Jizhe, household groom Youlong, crown prince's attendant Shao'an, and the rest—and killed them in their houses.

sentences.zh: 長子黃門郎元遷，為寧朔將軍，領千人於徐州擊虜，敕徐州刺史徐玄慶殺之。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanyuan, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was General Who Pacifies the North, leading a thousand men on campaign against the barbarians at Xuzhou—the edict ordered Xuzhou Inspector Xu Xuanqing to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest, Yuanyuan, gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was general who pacifies the north, leading a thousand men against the barbarians at Xuzhou; the edict ordered Xuzhou inspector Xu Xuanqing to kill him.

sentences.zh: 敬則招集配衣，二三日便發，欲劫前中書令何胤還為尚書令，長史王弄璋、司馬張思祖止之。

translations.literal: Jingze mustered troops and equipage; in two or three days he set out. He meant to seize former Secretariat Director He Yin and bring him back as Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Chief Clerk Wang Nongzhang and Chief of Staff Zhang Sinzu stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze gathered men and gear and marched within two or three days. He meant to seize the former director of the secretariat He Yin and make him director again; chief clerk Wang Nongzhang and chief of staff Zhang Sinzu held him back.

sentences.zh: 乃率實甲萬人過浙江，謂思祖曰：「應須作檄。

translations.literal: He then led ten thousand men in solid armor across the Zhe River and said to Sinzu: 「We need to draft a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He then led ten thousand men in real armor across the Zhe and told Sinzu, 「We must issue a proclamation.

sentences.zh: 」思祖曰：「公今自還朝，何用作此。

translations.literal: 」Sinzu said: 「My lord is returning to court of your own accord—what need for this?
translations.idiomatic: 」Sinzu said, 「My lord is going back to court of your own will—why write this?

sentences.zh: 」敬則乃止。

translations.literal: 」Jingze thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣輔國將軍前軍司馬左興盛、後軍將軍直閤將軍崔恭祖、輔國將軍劉山陽、龍驤將軍直閤將軍馬軍主胡松三千餘人，築壘于曲阿長岡，右僕射沈文季為持節都督，屯湖頭，備京口路。

translations.literal: The court sent Augmenting-the-State General and Vanguard Army Marshal Zuo Xingsheng, Rear Army General and Palace Gate General Cui Gongzu, Augmenting-the-State General Liu Shanyang, and Dragon-charger General and Palace Gate General and Cavalry Commandant Hu Song—more than three thousand men—to build ramparts at the long ridge of Qu'e. Vice Director Shen Wenji was Commissioner with full powers; he camped at Hutou to block the Jingkou road.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent augmenting-the-state general and vanguard army marshal Zuo Xingsheng, rear army general and palace gate general Cui Gongzu, augmenting-the-state general Liu Shanyang, and dragon-charger general, palace gate general, and cavalry commandant Hu Song—more than three thousand in all—to build works on the long ridge at Qu'e. Vice director Shen Wenji held the staff as commissioner with full powers and camped at Hutou to guard the Jingkou road.

sentences.zh: 敬則以舊將舉事，百姓擔篙荷鍤隨逐之，十餘万衆。

translations.literal: Jingze rose as an old general of renown; the common people shouldered poles and hoes and followed him—more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze rose as a famous old commander; common folk shouldered poles and spades and followed—more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 至晉陵，南沙人范脩化殺縣令公上延孫以應之。

translations.literal: Reaching Jinling, Fan Xiuhua of Nansha killed Magistrate Gongshang Yansun to answer him.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling, Fan Xiuhua of Nansha killed the magistrate Gongshang Yansun to join him.

sentences.zh: 敬則至武進陵口，慟哭乘肩輿而前。

translations.literal: Jingze came to the pass of the Wujin tombs, wept, and rode forward in a shoulder carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze came to the pass by the Wujin tombs, wept aloud, and went on in a shoulder litter.

sentences.zh: 遇興盛、山陽二砦，儘力攻之。

translations.literal: He met the two camps of Xingsheng and Shanyang and attacked with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He struck the two camps of Xingsheng and Shanyang with all he had.

sentences.zh: 興盛使軍人遙告敬則曰：「公兒死已盡，公持許底作？

translations.literal: Xingsheng had soldiers call out from afar to Jingze: 「Your sons are all dead—what do you mean to hold on to?
translations.idiomatic: Xingsheng had men shout across to Jingze, 「Your sons are all dead—what are you still holding to?

sentences.zh: 」官軍不敵欲退，而圍不開，各死戰。

translations.literal: 」The government troops could not match them and meant to retreat, but the encirclement would not break—each side fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: 」The government host could not stand and meant to pull back, but the ring would not open—both sides fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 胡松領馬軍突其後，白丁無器仗，皆驚散，敬則軍大敗。

translations.literal: Hu Song led the horse soldiers in a thrust at their rear; the common levies without weapons panicked and scattered—Jingze's army was utterly broken.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song drove the horse troops into their rear; unarmed levies broke in terror—Jingze's force collapsed.

sentences.zh: 敬則索馬，再上不得上，興盛軍容袁文曠斬之，傳首。

translations.literal: Jingze sought a horse but could not mount again. Xingsheng's Army Majordomo Yuan Wenkuan struck him down and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze called for a horse and could not get back into the saddle. Xingsheng's army majordomo Yuan Wenkuan cut him down and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 是時上疾已篤，敬則倉卒東起，朝廷震懼。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's illness was already grave; Jingze had risen hurriedly in the east, and the court was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already near death; Jingze had risen in haste in the east, and the court shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯在東宮，議欲叛，使人上屋望，見征虜亭失火，謂敬則至，急裝欲走。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Eastern Darkness at the Eastern Palace debated turning rebel; he sent men onto the roof to watch, saw the Zhengfu Pavilion catch fire, thought Jingze had arrived, and hurried to pack and flee.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis of Eastern Darkness at the Eastern Palace talked of rebelling; he sent men onto the roof to look, saw fire at the Zhengfu Pavilion, took it for Jingze's arrival, and rushed to dress and run.

sentences.zh: 有告敬則者，敬則曰：「檀公三十六策，走是上計。

translations.literal: When someone came to warn Jingze, Jingze said: 「Of Duke Tan's thirty-six stratagems, flight is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Jingze, he said: 「Among Duke Tan's thirty-six stratagems, running is the best of all.

sentences.zh: 汝父子唯應急走耳。

translations.literal: You father and son should only flee at once.」
translations.idiomatic: You and your son had best run for your lives—now.」

sentences.zh: 」敬則之來，聲勢甚盛，裁少日而敗，時年七十餘。

translations.literal: 」Jingze's rising had been loud in force, yet within a few days he was broken; he was then in his seventies.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jingze had marched east in thunder and numbers, yet within days he was undone; he was past seventy.

sentences.zh: 封左興盛新吳縣男，崔恭祖遂興縣男，劉山陽湘陰縣男，胡松沙陽縣男，各四百戶，賞平敬則也。

translations.literal: Zuo Xingsheng was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinwu, Cui Gongzu as Baron of Suixing, Liu Shanyang as Baron of Xiangyin, and Hu Song as Baron of Shayang, each with four hundred households, in reward for pacifying Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Xingsheng was made baron of Xinwu, Cui Gongzu baron of Suixing, Liu Shanyang baron of Xiangyin, and Hu Song baron of Shayang—four hundred households each—as reward for putting down Jingze.

sentences.zh: 又贈公上延孫為射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Gong Shangyansun was also posthumously made Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot by Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shangyansun was also given posthumous rank as colonel of the archers who shoot by sound.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達，南彭城人也。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda was a native of Nan Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda came from Nan Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武世，為張永前軍幢主。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of Song he served as chief of the vanguard pennons under Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu of Song he was chief of the forward pennons on Zhang Yong's staff.

sentences.zh: 景和中，以勞歷使使。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era, for merit he was repeatedly sent on missions.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe years his service won him repeated turns as envoy.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，以軍主隸徐州刺史劉懷珍北征，累至東海王板行參軍，員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he joined as army commander under the northern campaign of Xu Province inspector Liu Huaizhen, and rose in stages to acting staff officer on the Prince of Donghai's commission and to outer-office gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened he marched north as an army commander under Xu inspector Liu Huaizhen, and in time reached acting staff officer to the Prince of Donghai and outer-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，封彭澤縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pengze with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year four he was made viscount of Pengze at three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷馬頭、義陽二郡太守，羽林監，濮陽太守。

translations.literal: He served in turn as administrator of Matou and Yiyang, as inspector of the feathered forest, and as administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Matou and Yiyang in succession, held the feathered-forest inspectorship, and became administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 隸太祖討桂陽賊於新亭壘，劉勔大桁敗，賊進杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Under the Grand Ancestor he campaigned against the Guiyang rebels at the Xinting rampart; Liu Qin's great pontoon force was routed, and the rebels pressed into Old Woman Du's quarter.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Grand Ancestor against the Guiyang rebels at Xinting; Liu Qin's great bridge army was smashed, and the enemy drove into Old Woman Du's quarter.

sentences.zh: 及休範死，太祖欲還衛宮城，或諫太祖曰：「桂陽雖死，賊黨猶熾，人情難固，不可輕動。

translations.literal: When Xiufan died, the Grand Ancestor wished to return and guard the palace city; someone admonished the Grand Ancestor: 「Though Guiyang is dead, the rebel faction still burns hot; hearts are hard to hold—do not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiufan fell, the Grand Ancestor meant to fall back and hold the palace; an adviser urged him: 「Guiyang is dead, but his party still runs hot—the mood is brittle. Do not stir yet.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃止。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Ancestor thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Grand Ancestor held his ground.

sentences.zh: 遣顯達率司空參軍高敬祖自查浦渡淮緣石頭北道入承明門，屯東堂。

translations.literal: He sent Xianda to lead the Minister of Works's staff officer Gao Jingzu from Zhapu to cross the Huai, follow the Stone Hill northern road into the Chenming Gate, and encamp at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xianda with Gao Jingzu of the works staff to cross the Huai at Zhapu, take the northern road past Stone Hill into Chenming Gate, and camp in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 宮中恐動，得顯達至，乃稍定。

translations.literal: Inside the palace panic was rising; when Xianda arrived, it eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The palace was near panic; Xianda's arrival steadied it a little.

sentences.zh: 顯達出杜姥宅，大戰破賊。

translations.literal: Xianda went out from Old Woman Du's quarter and in a great battle broke the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda sallied from Old Woman Du's quarter and in heavy fighting routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 矢中左眼，拔箭而鏃不出，地黃村潘嫗善禁，先以釘釘柱，嫗禹步作氣，釘卽時出，乃禁顯達目中鏃出之。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his left eye; he pulled the shaft but the head would not come out. Pan the old woman of Dihuang village was skilled in taboo-magic; she first drove a nail into a pillar, paced in the Yu stride and gathered breath, and the nail came out at once—then she worked the charm and drew the arrowhead from Xianda's eye.
translations.idiomatic: A shaft struck his left eye; he drew it, but the head stayed fast. In Dihuang village old Pan knew forbidden arts: she drove a nail into a post, paced the Yu stride, breathed power into it, and the nail leapt free—then she charmed the head from Xianda's eye.

sentences.zh: 封豐城縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made marquis of Fengcheng at one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Raiding Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to general of raiding cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋為使持節、督廣交越三州湘州之廣興軍事、輔國將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，進號冠軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, superintendent of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, and Yue and in Guangxing of Xiang, General Who Assists the State, General Who Pacifies the Yue as central commandant, and Governor of Guang, with his title advanced to Champion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he bore the staff as commander of Guang, Jiao, and Yue and of Xiang's Guangxing, general who assists the state and central commandant pacifying the Yue, and governor of Guang—with his style raised to Champion.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，顯達遣軍援臺。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt rose, Xianda sent troops to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Xianda marched troops to the capital's aid.

sentences.zh: 長史到遁、司馬諸葛導謂顯達曰：「沈攸之擁衆百万，勝負之勢未可知。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Dao Dun and aide Zhuge Dao said to Xianda: 「Shen Youzhi holds a host of a million men; who will win is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Dao Dun and aide Zhuge Dao told him: 「Shen Youzhi fields a million men—the outcome is anyone's guess.

sentences.zh: 不如保境蓄衆，分遣信驛，密通彼此。

translations.literal: Better to hold your borders, gather your strength, and send couriers in secret to keep word passing between the two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Hold your province, hoard your men, and post secret riders to keep touch with both camps.

sentences.zh: 」顯達於座手斬之，遣表疏歸心太祖。

translations.literal: 」Xianda struck them down with his own hand at table, sent a memorial pledging his heart to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xianda cut them down where they sat and sent a memorial binding his loyalty to the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、左將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Bearer of the Staff and General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose to bearer of the staff and general of the left.

sentences.zh: 軍至巴丘，而沈攸之平。

translations.literal: His army reached Baqiu—and by then Shen Youzhi was already put down.
translations.idiomatic: His column reached Baqiu; Shen Youzhi was already broken.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍、左衛將軍，轉前將軍、太祖太尉左司馬。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Guard, then transferred to General of the Van and left chief of staff to the Grand Ancestor as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was named attendant cavalier-in-ordinary and general of the left guard, then general of the van and left chief of staff to the Grand Ancestor in his grand commandant's camp.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，為散騎常侍，左衛將軍，領衛尉。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, he became Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, General of the Left Guard, and concurrently Commandant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Qi regime he was attendant cavalier-in-ordinary and general of the left guard, and also commandant of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，遷中護軍，增邑千六百戶，轉護軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, Xianda was moved to Central Protector of the Army, his fief increased by one thousand six hundred households, and he was transferred to Protector-General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor ascended, Xianda became central protector of the army, gained one thousand six hundred more households on his fief, and was made protector-general of the army.

sentences.zh: 顯達啟讓，上答曰：「朝廷爵人以序。

translations.literal: Xianda memorialized to decline; the emperor answered: 「The court enfeoffs men in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda asked to stand down; the emperor replied: 「The court grants rank in its proper order.

sentences.zh: 卿忠發萬里，信誓如期，雖屠城殄國之勳，無以相加。

translations.literal: You set loyalty in motion ten thousand li away and kept your sworn word to the day—though one had the merit of razing cities and extinguishing states, nothing could be set above it.
translations.idiomatic: You pledged yourself from ten thousand li away and kept faith to the hour—even merit that razes cities and ends kingdoms could not stand above it.

sentences.zh: 此而不賞，典章何在！

translations.literal: If this is not rewarded, where do statutes and precedent stand!
translations.idiomatic: Reward less than this, and what becomes of law and precedent!

sentences.zh: 若必未宜爾，吾終不妄授。

translations.literal: If you truly deem it still unfitting, I will never grant it wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: If you still judge it unfit, I will not bestow it lightly.

sentences.zh: 於卿數士，意同家人，豈止於君臣邪？

translations.literal: With you and a few such men my heart is that of family—how could it stop at lord and minister alone?
translations.idiomatic: For you and a handful like you my heart is kin, not courtier alone—how could it be only lord and minister?

sentences.zh: 過明，與王、李俱祗召也。

translations.literal: Tomorrow at dawn you, Wang, and Li will all be summoned to attend.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn tomorrow you, Wang, and Li are all to present yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」上卽位後，御膳不宰牲，顯達上熊烝一盤，上卽以充飯。

translations.literal: 」After the emperor took the throne, the imperial kitchen did not slaughter animals for his meals; Xianda presented a dish of steamed bear, and the emperor ate it as his meal.
translations.idiomatic: 」Once enthroned, the emperor would have no beast killed for his table; Xianda sent up a plate of steamed bear, and he took it for his meal.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，虜寇壽陽，淮南江北百姓搔動。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan the northern enemy raided Shouyang, and the people north and south of the Huai in Huainan were thrown into unrest.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year two the northern enemy struck Shouyang; north and south of the Huai in Huainan the people quaked.

sentences.zh: 上以顯達為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兖州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor made Xianda Bearer of the Staff, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, commander of all military affairs in Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him bearer of the staff and attendant cavalier-in-ordinary, commander of Southern Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, general who pacifies the north, and governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 之鎮，虜退。

translations.literal: When he reached his post, the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He took up his command; the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 上敕顯達曰：「虜經破散後，當無復犯關理。

translations.literal: The emperor charged Xianda: 「After the enemy has been broken and scattered, they ought not to have reason to strike the passes again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Xianda: 「Once broken and scattered, the northerners should have no cause to test the passes again.

sentences.zh: 但國家邊防，自應過存備豫。

translations.literal: Yet the state's frontier defense should by rights be kept well prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the frontier must be held in more than name.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉二十七年後，江夏王作南兖，徙鎮盱眙，沈司空亦以孝建初鎮彼，政當以淮上要於廣陵耳。

translations.literal: After the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia in Song, the Prince of Jiangxia held Southern Yan and moved his garrison to Chuyang; the Minister of Works Shen likewise garrisoned there at the start of Xiaojian—policy should treat the Huai line as weightier than Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song's Yuanjia year twenty-seven the Prince of Jiangxia held Southern Yan and shifted his seat to Chuyang; Minister of Works Shen garrisoned there too at the opening of Xiaojian—the Huai frontier, not Guangling, was the hinge.

sentences.zh: 卿謂前代此處分云何？

translations.literal: What do you say of how earlier ages disposed this post?
translations.idiomatic: How do you read what earlier reigns did with this command?

sentences.zh: 今僉議皆云卿應據彼地，吾未能決。

translations.literal: Now the joint counsel is that you should hold that ground, but I have not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: Now every voice in council says you should take that ground, and I have not settled it.

sentences.zh: 乃當以擾動文武為勞。

translations.literal: It would only trouble the civil and military ranks.
translations.idiomatic: It would only weary court and camp alike.

sentences.zh: 若是公計，不得憚之。

translations.literal: If that is your settled counsel, I must not shrink from it.」
translations.idiomatic: If that is your firm advice, I cannot flinch from it.」

sentences.zh: 」事竟不行。

translations.literal: 」In the end the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: 」In the end nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 遷都督益寧二州軍事、安西將軍、益州刺史，領宋寧太守，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Yi, with concurrent office as Administrator of Songning, while Bearer of the Staff and Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to commander of Yi and Ning, general who pacifies the west, and governor of Yi, still holding Songning as administrator, with staff and attendant rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，進號鎮西。
