translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Xianda's title was advanced to General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended, Xianda's style rose to general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 益部山險，多不賓服。

translations.literal: In the Yibu region the mountains were dangerous and many would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yibu the mountains were sheer and treacherous, and many tribes would not bow.

sentences.zh: 大度村獠，前後刺史不能制，顯達遣使責其租賧，獠帥曰：「兩眼刺史尚不敢調我！

translations.literal: The Liao of Daidu village—prefects before and after had been unable to control them. Xianda sent envoys to demand rent and tribute. The Liao chief said: 「Even a Two-Eyes Governor never dared press me!
translations.idiomatic: At Daidu village the Liao had defied every inspector for years. Xianda sent men to collect rent and tribute. The Liao chief said, 「Even a Two-Eyes Governor never dared lean on me!

sentences.zh: 」遂殺其使。

translations.literal: 」They thereupon killed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: 」Then they killed the envoys.

sentences.zh: 顯達分部將吏，聲將出獵，夜往襲之，男女無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Xianda divided his officers and clerks, announced a hunting expedition, and struck by night—men and women, young and old, all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda split his command, cried a hunt, and fell on them by night—man, woman, child, none spared the blade.

sentences.zh: 自此山夷震服。

translations.literal: From then on the mountain tribes were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: After that the mountain tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 廣漢賊司馬龍駒據郡反，顯達又討平之。

translations.literal: In Guanghan the bandit Sima Longju seized the commandery and rebelled; Xianda pacified him as well.
translations.idiomatic: At Guanghan the rebel Sima Longju seized the commandery and rose; Xianda put him down again.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，徵為侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was summoned as Palace Attendant and General of the Protecting Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year two he was called in as palace attendant and general of the protecting army.

sentences.zh: 顯達累任在外，經太祖之憂，及見世祖，流涕悲咽，上亦泣，心甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Xianda had long served in the provinces and passed through the Grand Ancestor's mourning; when he at last saw Emperor Wu he wept until he choked, and the emperor wept too—the court was deeply pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda had long held posts abroad and lived through the Grand Ancestor's mourning; when he met Emperor Wu at last he wept until he could not speak, and the emperor wept with him—the throne was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 五年，荒人桓天生自稱桓玄宗族，與雍、司二州界蠻虜相扇動，據南陽故城。

translations.literal: In year five the wild man Huan Tiansheng styled himself kin to the house of Huan Xuan and, with the tribal allies along the Yong and Si borders, stirred rebellion and seized the old city of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year five the wild man Huan Tiansheng claimed descent from Huan Xuan, roused the tribal bands on the Yong and Si frontiers, and seized old Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 上遣顯達假節，率征虜將軍戴僧靜等水軍向宛、葉，雍、司衆軍受顯達節度。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Xianda with ceremonial authority, leading the Conquering Barbarians general Dai Sengjing and the river force toward Wan and Ye; all armies of Yong and Si fell under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Xianda the staff and sent him with Dai Sengjing, general who conquers the barbarians, and the river fleet toward Wan and Ye; every host of Yong and Si answered to him.

sentences.zh: 天生率虜衆萬餘人攻舞陰，舞陰戍主輔國將軍殷公愍擊殺其副張麒麟，天生被瘡退走。

translations.literal: Tiansheng led more than ten thousand tribal fighters against Wuyin; the garrison commander Yin Gongmin, General Who Assists the State, killed his lieutenant Zhang Qilin, and Tiansheng, wounded, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng led ten thousand-odd tribesmen against Wuyin; the garrison chief Yin Gongmin, general who assists the state, cut down his lieutenant Zhang Qilin, and Tiansheng, wounded, ran.

sentences.zh: 仍以顯達為使持節、散騎常持、都督雍梁南北秦郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、鎮北將軍，領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianda was given the staff, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, overall commander for Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingling in Ying, and Sui in Si, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda received the staff, was made regular attendant of the scattered riders and overall commander of Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, Jingling in Ying, and Sui in Si, general who pacifies the north, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 顯達進據舞陽城，遣僧靜等先進，與天生及虜再戰，大破之，官軍還。

translations.literal: Xianda advanced and held Wuyang city, sent Sengjing ahead, fought Tiansheng and the tribes twice, shattered them, and the government army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda moved up and took Wuyang, sent Sengjing forward, met Tiansheng and the tribes twice, broke them utterly, and the government host drew back.

sentences.zh: 數月，天生復出攻舞陰，殷公愍破之，天生還竄荒中，遂城、平氏、白土三城賊稍稍降散。

translations.literal: Months later Tiansheng came out again against Wuyin; Yin Gongmin defeated him, and Tiansheng fled back into the wilds; the rebels of Suicheng, Pingshi, and Baitu gradually surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Tiansheng struck Wuyin again; Yin Gongmin routed him and he fled into the wilds; rebels at Suicheng, Pingshi, and Baitu slowly surrendered and melted away.

sentences.zh: 八年，進號征北將軍。

translations.literal: In year eight he was advanced to General Who Conquers the North.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he was raised to general who conquers the north.

sentences.zh: 其年，仍遷侍中、鎮軍將軍，尋加中領軍。

translations.literal: That same year he was moved to Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army, and soon added Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was shifted to palace attendant and general who guards the army, and soon made central army commander as well.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州諸軍事、征南大將軍、江州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He went out with the staff as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, overall commander of Jiangzhou, General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Jiangzhou, with one suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He went out with the staff as regular attendant of the scattered riders, overall commander of Jiangzhou, general who conquers the south, and inspector of Jiangzhou, with one suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 顯達謙厚有智計，自以人微位重，每遷官，常有愧懼之色。

translations.literal: Xianda was humble in manner and full of stratagem; coming from low birth to high rank, at every promotion he wore shame and fear on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda was modest, thick, and shrewd; a man of humble roots in a heavy office, he showed shame and dread at every new seal.

sentences.zh: 有子十餘人，誡之曰：「我本志不及此，汝等勿以富貴陵人！

translations.literal: He had more than ten sons and warned them: 「My ambition never reached this height—you must not lord your wealth over others!
translations.idiomatic: He had more than ten sons and warned them, 「My heart never aimed this high—do not bully the world with your riches!

sentences.zh: 」家旣豪富，諸子與王敬則諸兒，竝精車牛，麗服飾。

translations.literal: 」The house was already rich; his sons and Wang Jingze's sons alike kept fine oxen and carriages and splendid dress.
translations.idiomatic: 」The house was already wealthy; his sons and Wang Jingze's sons alike drove matched cattle and wore bright gear.

sentences.zh: 當世快牛稱陳世子青，王三郎烏，呂文顯折角，江瞿曇白鼻。

translations.literal: The age's famed fast oxen were called Chen the Heir's Blue, Wang Third-Son Crow, Lu Wenxian Bent-Horn, and Jiang Qutan White-Nose.
translations.idiomatic: The age's swiftest oxen were Chen the Heir's Blue, Wang Third-Son Crow, Lu Wenxian Bent-Horn, and Jiang Qutan White-Nose.

sentences.zh: 顯達謂其子曰：「麈尾扇是王謝家物，汝不須捉此自逐。」

translations.literal: Xianda told his sons: 「The deer-tail fan belongs to the houses of Wang and Xie—you need not clutch that fashion for yourselves.」
translations.idiomatic: Xianda told his sons, 「Deer-tail fans are Wang and Xie playthings—you need not chase that fashion yourselves.」

sentences.zh: 十一年秋，虜動，詔屯樊城。

translations.literal: In the autumn of year eleven the northern enemy moved; an edict ordered him to camp at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, autumn, the northern enemy stirred; he was ordered to hold Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖遺詔，卽本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's testamentary edict, Xianda kept his present rank with Opening Palace parity of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's deathbed edict left him at his present rank with opening-palace parity of the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，遷侍中、車騎將軍，開府如故，置兵佐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was moved to Palace Attendant and General of the Flying Cavalry, opening palace as before, with military staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year one he became palace attendant and general of the flying cavalry, his opening palace unchanged, with a full military staff.

sentences.zh: 豫廢鬱林之勳，延興元年，為司空，進爵公，增邑千戶，甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: For his merit in deposing Yulin, in Yanxing year one he was made Minister of Works, advanced to duke, fief increased by one thousand households, and fifty armed guards permitted in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: For helping cast down Yulin, in Yanxing year one he was made minister of works, raised to duke, given a thousand added households, and fifty armed guards in the hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗卽位，進太尉，侍中如故，改封鄱陽郡公，邑三千戶，加兵二百人，給油絡車。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Xianda was advanced to Grand Commandant, Palace Attendant as before, re-enfeoffed Duke of Poyang with three thousand households, two hundred added guards, and granted an oil-mesh carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Xianda was made grand commandant, palace attendant as before, re-enfeoffed duke of Poyang with three thousand households, two hundred added guards, and an oil-mesh carriage.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，虜攻徐、司，詔顯達出頓，往來新亭白下，以為聲勢。

translations.literal: In Jianwu year two the northern enemy attacked Xu and Si; Xianda was ordered out to encamp, shuttling between Xinting and Baixia to lend weight to the defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year two the northern enemy struck Xu and Si; Xianda was sent out to hold the line, moving between Xinting and Baixia to swell the show of force.

sentences.zh: 上欲悉除高、武諸孫，微言問顯達，答曰：「此等豈足介慮。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to eliminate all descendants of the Gao and Wu lines and obliquely probed Xianda, who answered: 「Such folk are scarcely worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to wipe out every descendant of the Gao and Wu houses and sounded Xianda, who said, 「That lot is hardly worth a worry.

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: 」The emperor thereupon stayed his hand.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor let the plan drop.

sentences.zh: 顯達建武世心懷不安，深自貶匿，車乘朽故，導從鹵簿，皆用羸小，不過十數人。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era Xianda's heart knew no peace; he lowered himself deep in self-effacement—carriages rotting, escorts and insignia all the puniest men, never more than a dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwu Xianda lived in dread and hid himself low—rotting carriages, escorts and insignia all the weakest men, never a dozen in all.

sentences.zh: 侍宴，酒後啟上曰：「臣年已老，富貴已足，唯少枕枕死，特就陛下乞之。

translations.literal: At court feast, drunk, he addressed the throne: 「I am old, wealth enough; only a death in my bed still eludes me—and I come specially to beg it of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: At a court feast, drunk, he told the throne, 「I am old and have wealth enough; only a pillow-death still eludes me—and I come now to beg it of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上失色曰：「公醉矣。

translations.literal: 」The emperor blanched and said: 「You are drunk.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor went pale and said, 「You are drunk.

sentences.zh: 」以年禮告退，不許。

translations.literal: 」He asked to retire on grounds of age; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: 」He asked leave on grounds of age; it was refused.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，顯達督平北將軍崔慧景衆軍四萬，圍南鄉堺馬圈城，去襄陽三百里，攻之四十日。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan year one Xianda oversaw Pacifying North general Cui Huijing's combined armies—forty thousand men—and besieged the horse-pen city on the Nanxiang border, three hundred li from Xiangyang; the assault lasted forty days.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year one Xianda directed Cui Huijing, general who pacifies the north, and forty thousand men to ring the horse-pen city on the Nanxiang border, three hundred li from Xiangyang; the siege ran forty days.

sentences.zh: 虜食盡，啖死人肉及樹皮。

translations.literal: The enemy's grain ran out; they ate the flesh of the dead and tree bark.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's grain gave out; they ate the dead and gnawed bark.

sentences.zh: 外圍旣急，虜突走，斬獲千計。

translations.literal: The outer ring tightened; the enemy broke out in a rush—beheadings and captures numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The ring closed tight; the enemy burst out—slain and taken ran to the thousands.

sentences.zh: 官軍競取城中絹，不復窮追。

translations.literal: Government troops scrambled for silk in the city and would not pursue further.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fought over the city's silk and would not chase further.

sentences.zh: 顯達入據其城，遣軍主庄丘黑進取南鄉縣，故順陽郡治也。

translations.literal: Xianda entered and held the place, sent the army commander Zhuangqiu Hei to take Nanxiang county—the old seat of Shunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda entered and held the city, sent the army commander Zhuangqiu Hei to take Nanxiang county, the old seat of Shunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 虜主元宏自領十餘萬騎奄至，顯達引軍渡水西據鷹子山築城，人情沮敗。

translations.literal: The northern ruler Yuan Hong himself led more than a hundred thousand horsemen in a sudden strike; Xianda drew his force west of the river to Eagle-Kite Hill and threw up a wall, but morale collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The northern ruler Yuan Hong came in person with a hundred thousand-odd horsemen; Xianda pulled his host west of the water to Eagle-Kite Hill and walled it, but hearts broke.

sentences.zh: 虜兵甚急，軍主崔恭祖、胡松以烏布幔盛顯達，數人擔之，逕道從分磧山出均水口，臺軍緣道奔退，死者三万餘人。

translations.literal: The enemy pressed hard; army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song wrapped Xianda in a black-cloth canopy and bore him on several men's shoulders along a mountain track through Split-Ridge Hill out to Jun mouth; the capital army fled along the road—dead passed thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pressed hot; army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song swathed Xianda in a black-cloth canopy and had a few men carry him by a back path over Split-Ridge Hill to Jun mouth; the capital host fled along the road—more than thirty thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 左軍將張千戰死，追贈游擊將軍。

translations.literal: Left army officer Zhang Qian died in battle; posthumously made General of the Rapid Attack.
translations.idiomatic: Left army officer Zhang Qian fell in the fight; posthumously he was made general of the rapid attack.

sentences.zh: 顯達素有威名，著於蠻虜，至是大損喪焉。

translations.literal: Xianda had long held awe among the tribes; now his name was grievously dimmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda's dread name had long run among the tribes; now it was grievously broken.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞范岫奏免顯達官，朝議優詔答曰：「昔衛、霍出塞，往往無功，馮、鄧入關，有時虧喪。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Fan Xiu memorialized to strip Xianda of office; court deliberation answered with a gentle edict: 「Of old, when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the pass they often won nothing; when Feng Yi and Deng Yu entered the passes they sometimes met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Fan Xiu asked that Xianda be stripped of office; the court answered with a gentle edict: 「In old days Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes and often won nothing; Feng Yi and Deng Yu entered the passes and sometimes met ruin.

sentences.zh: 況公規謨肅舉，期寄兼深、見可知難，無損威略。

translations.literal: How much more so with you—your plans are stern and your charge from the throne runs deep; hardship in plain sight cannot touch your renown.
translations.idiomatic: How much more for you, whose counsel is grave and whose charge from the throne runs deep—when hardship shows plain upon the field, your prestige is not lessened.

sentences.zh: 方振遠圖，廓清朔土。

translations.literal: Now is the hour to shake the distant plan and sweep clear the northern soil.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the hour to shake the far design and sweep the northern soil clean.

sentences.zh: 雖執憲有常，非所得議。

translations.literal: Though the law holds its course, this is not a matter for such debate.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law has its course, this is not a matter for such debate.

sentences.zh: 」顯達表解職，不許，求降號，又不許。

translations.literal: 」Xianda memorialized to resign; denied. He asked to lower his rank; denied again.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xianda memorialized to quit; it was refused. He asked to lower his rank; that too was refused.

sentences.zh: 以顯達為都督江州軍事、江州刺史，鎮盆城，持節本官如故。

translations.literal: Xianda was made overall commander of Jiangzhou, Inspector of Jiangzhou, with garrison at Pen city, staff and other offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda was made overall commander of Jiangzhou, inspector of Jiangzhou, garrisoned at Pen city, with the staff and his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，王敬則事起，始安王遙光啟明帝慮顯達為變，欲追軍還，事尋平，乃寢。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze's rebellion first broke out, the Prince of Shian Yao Guang warned Mingdi that Xianda might turn rebel and urged recalling the army; the affair soon settled and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze first rose, the Prince of Shian Yao Guang warned Mingdi that Xianda might turn and urged the army recalled; the affair soon settled and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 顯達亦懷危怖。

translations.literal: Xianda also harbored fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda, too, lived in fear and dread.

sentences.zh: 及東昏立，彌不樂還京師，得此授，甚喜。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne, he was all the less willing to return to the capital; receiving this appointment, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghun ascended, he was even less eager to go back to the capital; this new posting delighted him.

sentences.zh: 尋加領征南大將軍，給三望車。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given concurrent command as General Who Campaigns South, with a three-peacock carriage awarded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made General Who Campaigns South in concurrent command, with the gift of a three-peacock carriage.

sentences.zh: 顯達聞京師大相殺戮，又知徐孝嗣等皆死，傳聞當遣兵襲江州，顯達懼禍，十一月十五日，舉兵。

translations.literal: Xianda heard of the great slaughter in the capital, and learned that Xu Xiaosi and the rest were all dead; rumors held that troops would be sent to strike Jiangzhou—Xianda feared disaster, and on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month he raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda heard that the capital was awash in killing, that Xu Xiaosi and his circle were dead, and that an army might be sent against Jiangzhou. Dreading ruin, on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month he rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 令長史庾弘遠、司馬徐虎龍與朝貴書曰：

translations.literal: He ordered Chief Clerk Yu Hongyuan and Marshal Xu Hulong to write a letter to the court nobles, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He had Chief Clerk Yu Hongyuan and Marshal Xu Hulong address a letter to the great men of court:

sentences.zh: 諸君足下：我太祖高皇帝叡哲自天，超人作聖，屬彼宋季，綱紀自頓，應禪從民，遘此基業。

translations.literal: Gentlemen all: Our founding Grandfather, the High Emperor, was wise and perspicacious as if heaven-given, transcending ordinary men to become sage; when the Song dynasty's final season came and its discipline collapsed, he accepted the abdication following the people's will and inherited this foundation.
translations.idiomatic: 「Gentlemen: Our founding Grandfather, the High Emperor, was wise beyond measure, heaven-touched, raised above common men to sagehood. When the Song line failed and its order crumbled, he took the abdication the people offered and won this foundation.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝昭略通遠，克纂洪嗣，四關罷嶮，三河靜塵。

translations.literal: Our Ancestor, the Martial Emperor, had far-reaching strategic brilliance and succeeded to the great succession; the four passes were eased of peril and the three rivers stilled of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Our Ancestor, the Martial Emperor, saw far and grasped wide; he took up the great succession, stilled the four frontier passes, and laid the dust of the three rivers.

sentences.zh: 鬱林海陵，頓孤負荷。

translations.literal: At Yulin and Hailing the throne was suddenly left orphaned and burdened.
translations.idiomatic: At Yulin and Hailing the throne stood suddenly orphaned, the weight on one pair of shoulders.

sentences.zh: 明帝英聖，紹建中興。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was heroic and sage, continuing and building the mid-dynasty revival.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was heroic and bright, and raised the mid-dynasty revival.

sentences.zh: 至乎後主，行悖三才，琴橫凷席，繡積麻筵，淫犯先宮，穢興閨闥，皇陛為市廛之所，雕房起征戰之門。

translations.literal: As for the later sovereign, his conduct violated the three powers; he strung the zither across the overturned mat, heaped embroidery on the hemp banquet, violated the former palace in lust, and defiled the inner quarters; the imperial steps became a marketplace and the carved chambers gates of war.
translations.idiomatic: As for the present lord, his ways overturn the three powers: the zither laid across the upended mat, brocade piled on the hemp feast, lust that violated the former palace, filth that rose in the inner quarters—the imperial steps turned marketplace, the carved chambers opened as gates of war.

sentences.zh: 任非華尚，寵必寒廝。

translations.literal: Appointments were not drawn from the flower of talent; favor fell only on cold kitchen servants.
translations.idiomatic: Office went not to the finest men; favor fell only on kitchen drudges from the cold hearth.

sentences.zh: 江僕射兄弟，忠言屬薦，正諫繁興，覆族之誅，於斯而至。

translations.literal: Vice-Director Jiang and his brothers offered loyal words again and again and straight remonstrance in abundance—the punishment that wiped out their clan arrived at last.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Director Jiang and his brothers spoke loyalty again and again, remonstrance without end—and at last came the sentence that wiped out their house.

sentences.zh: 故乃犴噬之刑，四剽於海路，家門之釁，一起於中都。

translations.literal: Thus the devouring execution spread to four quarters along the sea-roads, and the disaster to one's house arose first in the central capital.
translations.idiomatic: So the cage-and-devour punishments ran to the four corners of the sea-roads, and the ruin of a house began first in the central capital.

sentences.zh: 蕭、劉二領軍，竝升御座，共稟遺詔，宗戚之苦，諒不足談，《渭陽》之悲，何辜至此。

translations.literal: The two Army Commanders-in-Chief Xiao and Liu both ascended the imperial seat and together received the testamentary edict—the bitterness of the imperial kin need not be spoken of; the grief of the Wei Yang ode—what crime brought them to this?
translations.idiomatic: Army Commanders-in-Chief Xiao and Liu were both forced to the imperial seat and made to receive the deathbed edict together—the anguish of the imperial kin scarcely bears telling; the grief of the Wei Yang ode—what guilt brought them here?

sentences.zh: 徐司空歷葉忠榮，清簡流世，匡翼之功未著，傾宗之罰已彰。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xu had loyal merit through generations and a pure, simple name in his age; his power to brace and support was not yet shown when the punishment that overturned his clan was already plain.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xu bore loyal honor through generations, a pure name in his age; his power to brace the throne had not yet shown when the sentence that overturned his clan was already plain.

sentences.zh: 沈僕射年在懸車，將念机杖，歡歌園藪，絕影朝門，忽招陵上之罰，何萬古之傷哉！

translations.literal: Vice-Director Shen was of an age to hang up the chariot; he meant to take up armrest and staff and sing in garden and marsh, leaving no shadow at the court gate—yet suddenly he met punishment on the mound; what sorrow for ten thousand ages!
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Director Shen had reached the age to hang up the chariot, to take staff and cane and sing in garden and marsh, leaving no shadow at the court gate—yet suddenly he met the mound's punishment. What wound for ten thousand ages!

sentences.zh: 遂使紫臺之路，絕縉紳之儔；

translations.literal: Thus the road to the Purple Terrace was cut off from the girdled nobles;
translations.idiomatic: So the road to the Purple Terrace was cut off from girdled nobles;

sentences.zh: 纓組之閤，罷金、張之胤。

translations.literal: the hall of tasseled seals ceased the line of Jin and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: the hall of tasseled cords saw the line of Jin and Zhang end.

sentences.zh: 悲哉！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 蟬冕為賤寵之服，嗚呼！

translations.literal: The cicada crown became the dress of petty favor; alas!
translations.idiomatic: The cicada crown became the garb of base favor—alas!

sentences.zh: 皇陛列劫豎之坐。

translations.literal: on the imperial steps sat the seat of the robber-serf.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial steps stood the seats of robber-thralls.

sentences.zh: 且天人同怨，乾象變錯，往歲三州流血，今者五地自動。

translations.literal: Moreover, heaven and men share one wrath, and the celestial signs shift awry; in past years three provinces bled; this year five regions quake of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men share one wrath; the sky-signs turn awry. Three provinces bled in years past; five lands quake of themselves this year.

sentences.zh: 昔漢池異色，胥王因之見廢；

translations.literal: Of old, when the Han pool changed color, the Prince of Jin was deposed because of it;
translations.idiomatic: Of old, when the Han pool changed color, the Prince of Jin was cast aside for it;

sentences.zh: 吳郡暫震，步生以為奸幸。

translations.literal: when Wu commandery shook for a time, Bu Sheng took it for the work of a treacherous favorite.
translations.idiomatic: when Wu commandery trembled for a season, Bu Sheng read it as the doing of a treacherous favorite.

sentences.zh: 況事隆于往怪，釁倍於前虐，此而未廢，孰不可興？

translations.literal: How much more when events surpass the marvels of the past and offenses double the tyranny before—if this is not cast aside, what may not be raised?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the matter outdoes the marvels of old and the guilt doubles the tyranny before—if this is not cast down, what may not be raised up?

sentences.zh: 王僕射、王領軍、崔護軍，中維簡正，逆念剖心。

translations.literal: Vice-Director Wang, Army Commander Wang, and Protector-General Cui stand firm at the center with upright simplicity, their opposing thoughts laid open like a split heart.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-Director Wang, Army Commander Wang, and Protector-General Cui hold the center with upright simplicity, their contrary will laid open as a heart split in two.

sentences.zh: 蕭衛尉、蔡詹事、沈左衛，各負良家，共傷時嶮。

translations.literal: Chamberlain Xiao, Household Steward Cai, and Left Guards General Shen each come of good houses and together mourn the peril of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Chamberlain Xiao, Household Steward Cai, and Left Guards General Shen each spring from good houses and together grieve the age's peril.

sentences.zh: 先朝遺舊，志在名節，同列丹書，要同義舉。

translations.literal: Survivors of the former court set their will on name and integrity; they share the same red-scroll pledge and will join the righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of the former court set their hearts on name and integrity; they share one red-scroll pledge and mean to rise together in righteousness.

sentences.zh: 建安殿下秀德沖遠，寔允神器。

translations.literal: His Highness of Jian'an has refined virtue, lofty and far-seen—truly fit for the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: His Highness of Jian'an bears refined virtue, lofty and far-seen—truly fit for the sacred vessel.

sentences.zh: 昏明之舉，往聖流言。

translations.literal: The acts that discern bright from dark—former sages left them in their teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The deed that sorts dark from bright—former sages left it in their teachings.

sentences.zh: 今忝役戎驅，亟請乞路。

translations.literal: Now, bearing the shame of war and march, I urgently ask a clear road.
translations.idiomatic: Now, shamed by war and forced march, I urgently beg a clear road.

sentences.zh: 須京塵一靜，西迎大駕，歌舞太平，不亦佳哉！

translations.literal: Once the capital's dust is stilled I shall meet the great carriage in the west; to sing and dance in peace—is that not fine?
translations.idiomatic: When the capital's dust is stilled I shall meet the great carriage in the west and sing and dance in peace—is that not fine?

sentences.zh: 裴豫州宿遣誠言，久懷慷慨，計其勁兵，已登淮路；

translations.literal: Pei of Yuzhou has long sent words of sincere intent and borne generous resolve; I reckon his elite troops have already marched on the Huai road.
translations.idiomatic: Pei of Yuzhou has long sent words of sincere intent and kept a generous heart; I reckon his crack troops are already on the Huai road.

sentences.zh: 申司州志節堅明，分見迎合，總勒偏率，殿我而進；

translations.literal: Shen of Sizhou has will and integrity firm and bright; his officers meet us in division, gathering irregular forces to screen my rear while advancing;
translations.idiomatic: Shen of Sizhou has will and integrity firm and bright; his officers meet us in division, gather irregular forces, and screen my rear as we advance;

sentences.zh: 蕭雍州、房僧寄竝已纂邁，旌鼓將及；

translations.literal: Xiao of Yongzhou and Fang Sengji have both already taken up the succession; their banners and drums are about to arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao of Yongzhou and Fang Sengji have both already taken up the succession; their banners and drums are nearly here;

sentences.zh: 南兖州司馬崔恭祖壯烈超群，嘉驛屢至，佇聽烽諜，共成唇齒；

translations.literal: Sima Cui Gongzu of Southern Yanzhou is fiercely heroic beyond the common run; good dispatches come again and again—we await the beacon reports and will be lip to tooth together;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Cui Gongzu of Southern Yanzhou is fierce beyond the common run; good dispatches come again and again—we wait on the beacon reports and will be lip to tooth;

sentences.zh: 荊郢行事蕭、張二賢，莫不案劍餐風，橫戈待節。

translations.literal: The acting officers of Jing and Ying, the two worthies Xiao and Zhang, all draw sword and sup wind, level spear and wait the moment.
translations.idiomatic: The acting officers of Jing and Ying, the two worthies Xiao and Zhang, all lay hand to sword, sup the wind, level spear, and wait the moment.

sentences.zh: 關畿蕃守之儔，孰非義侶！

translations.literal: Who among the frontier guards of the passes and marches is not a comrade in righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier guards of the passes and marches—who is not a comrade in the righteous cause!

sentences.zh: 我太尉公體道合聖，杖德脩文，神武橫於七伐，雄略震於九綱。

translations.literal: Our Grand Preceptor in body joins the Way with sageness, upholds virtue and cultivates letters; divine martial prowess spans the seven campaigns, heroic strategy shakes the nine principles.
translations.idiomatic: Our Grand Preceptor joins the Way with sageness in his person, upholds virtue and cultivates letters; divine martial prowess spans the seven campaigns, heroic strategy shakes the nine principles.

sentences.zh: 是乃從彼英序，還抗社稷。

translations.literal: Thus he follows that glorious order and returns to shield the altars.
translations.idiomatic: So he follows that glorious order and comes back to hold the altars.

sentences.zh: 本欲鳴笳細錫，無勞戈刃；

translations.literal: I had meant to sound the reed-pipe and bestow fine gifts, without troubling blade or spear;
translations.idiomatic: I had meant only to sound the reed-pipe and grant fine gifts, without calling on blade or spear;

sentences.zh: 但忠黨有心，節義難遣。

translations.literal: but the loyal party has its will and integrity's dictates cannot be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: but the loyal party has its will, and the dictates of integrity cannot be sent away.

sentences.zh: 信次之間，森然十萬。

translations.literal: Between one trust and the next, ranks stand close at a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Between one credence camp and the next, ranks stand close at a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 飛旍咽于九派，列艦迷於三川，此蓋捧海澆螢，烈火消凍耳。

translations.literal: Flying banners choke the nine branches; lined warships blur the three rivers—this is merely cupping the sea to douse a firefly or a fierce blaze melting frost.
translations.idiomatic: Flying banners choke the nine branches; lined warships blur the three rivers—this is only cupping the sea to douse a firefly, a fierce blaze to melt frost.

sentences.zh: 吾子其擇善而從之，無令竹帛空為後人笑也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen must choose what is good and follow it; do not let bamboo and silk stand empty only for later men to laugh.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must choose what is good and follow it; do not let bamboo and silk stand empty for later men to laugh.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣後軍將軍胡松、驍騎將軍李叔獻水軍據梁山；

translations.literal: The court sent Rear Army General Hu Song and Raiding Cavalry General Li Shuxian with a water force to hold Liangshan;
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Rear Army General Hu Song and Raiding Cavalry General Li Shuxian with a water host to hold Liangshan;

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍左興盛假節，加征虜將軍，督前鋒軍事，屯新亭；

translations.literal: Left Guards General Zuo Xingsheng with provisional staff, added as General Who Subdues the Enemy, supervising vanguard military affairs, camped at Xinting;
translations.idiomatic: Left Guards General Zuo Xingsheng held the staff in commission, was further named General Who Subdues the Enemy, supervised vanguard affairs, and camped at Xinting;

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍驍騎將軍徐世摽領兵屯杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Assistant-State General and Raiding Cavalry General Xu Shibiao led troops to camp at Du Lao's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant-State General and Raiding Cavalry General Xu Shibiao led troops to camp at Du Lao's residence.

sentences.zh: 顯達率衆數千人發尋陽，與胡松戰於採石，大破之，京邑震恐。

translations.literal: Xianda led several thousand men from Xunyang and fought Hu Song at Caishi, routing him utterly; the capital trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda led several thousand men out of Xunyang and fought Hu Song at Caishi, breaking him utterly; the capital shook with fear.

sentences.zh: 十二月十三日，顯達至新林築城壘，左興盛率衆軍為拒戰之計。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month Xianda reached Xinlin and built ramparts and stockades; Zuo Xingsheng led the mass of troops to plan defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month Xianda came to Xinlin and built ramparts and stockades; Zuo Xingsheng led the host to lay plans of defense.

sentences.zh: 其夜，顯達多置屯火于岸側，潛軍渡取石頭北上襲宮城，遇風失曉，十四日平旦，數千人登落星崗。

translations.literal: That night Xianda set many beacon fires along the shore, secretly sent troops across to take Shitou and strike north to raid the palace city; they met wind and lost the dawn hour; on the fourteenth at daybreak several thousand men climbed Falling Star Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xianda lined the bank with beacon fires, slipped troops across to seize Shitou, and drove north to strike the palace; wind and mist cost them the hour—at dawn on the fourteenth several thousand men stood on Falling Star Ridge.

sentences.zh: 新亭軍望火，謂顯達猶在，旣而奔歸赴救，屯城南。

translations.literal: The Xinting army saw the fires and thought Xianda was still there; then they ran back to rescue, camping south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinting force saw the blaze and took Xianda to be still in camp; they wheeled back to the rescue and pitched south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 宮掖大駭，閉門守備。

translations.literal: The palace quarters were greatly alarmed; gates were shut and defenses manned.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace panicked; gates were barred and the guard stood to arms.

sentences.zh: 顯達馬槊從步軍數百人，于西州前與臺軍戰，再合，大勝，手殺數人，槊折，官軍繼至，顯達不能抗，退走至西州烏榜村，為騎官趙潭注槊刺落馬，斬之於籬側，血涌湔籬，似淳于伯之被刑也。

translations.literal: Xianda with horse-lance led several hundred foot soldiers; before Xizhou they fought the capital army, twice engaged, won a great victory, personally killed several men; the lance broke; government troops kept coming; Xianda could not hold; he retreated to Wubang Village west of Xizhou; cavalry officer Zhao Tan drove his lance into him and knocked him from his horse; he was beheaded beside a hedge; blood gushed and washed the hedge, like Chunyu Bo under the headsman.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda on horseback with lance led a few hundred foot; before Xizhou he met the capital host twice and broke them, killing several men himself until the lance snapped; fresh government troops poured in and he could not stand; he fell back to Wubang hamlet west of Xizhou, where cavalry officer Zhao Tan thrust him from the saddle with his lance and cut off his head by a hedge—blood surged and sluiced the fence like Chunyu Bo at the block.

sentences.zh: 時年七十二。

translations.literal: He was seventy-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 顯達在江州，遇疾不治，尋而自差，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: When Xianda was in Jiangzhou he fell ill and did not seek treatment; soon he recovered on his own, but was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: While Xianda held Jiangzhou he took ill and would not call a physician; he mended of himself, yet the omen sat ill with him.

sentences.zh: 是冬連大雪，梟首於朱雀，而雪不集之。

translations.literal: That winter snow fell continuously; his head was displayed at Zhuque, yet snow did not settle on it.
translations.idiomatic: That winter snow fell again and again; his head was spiked at the Vermilion Bird Gate, and the snow would not lie on it.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: His sons were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：光武功臣所以能終其身名者，非唯不任職事，亦以繼奉明、章，心尊正嫡，君安乎上，臣習乎下。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The reason Guangwu's meritorious ministers could preserve their persons and names to the end was not only that they did not hold active duties, but also that they served Ming and Zhang in succession, honored the legitimate heir in heart, the lord was secure above and subjects habituated below.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Guangwu's fighting men kept skin and fame to the grave not only because they left office, but because they served Ming and Zhang in turn, bowed to the rightful heir, the throne rested easy above and the court below knew its place.

sentences.zh: 王、陳拔迹奮飛，則建元、永明之運；

translations.literal: Wang and Chen rose from humble origins and soared—that was the fortune of Jianyuan and Yongming;
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Chen clawed up from nothing—that was Jianyuan and Yongming;

sentences.zh: 身極鼎將，則建武、永元之朝。

translations.literal: when they reached the pinnacle as chief ministers—that was the court of Jianwu and Yongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: when they topped the realm as chief ministers—that was Jianwu and Yongyuan.

sentences.zh: 勳非往時，位踰昔等，禮授雖重，情分不交。

translations.literal: Their merit was not as in former times, their rank exceeded former peers; ceremonial grants though heavy, emotional bonds did not connect.
translations.idiomatic: Merit no longer matched the old days, rank outran old peers; rites and gifts weighed heavy, yet feeling never met.

sentences.zh: 加以主猜政亂，危亡慮及，舉手扞頭，人思自免。

translations.literal: Add to this the sovereign's suspicion and political chaos, the thought of ruin pressing upon them—raise hand to shield head, each man thinking only how to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Add a suspicious throne and a broken polity, ruin in every mind—hands went to heads, each man scheming only his own escape.

sentences.zh: 干戈旣用，誠淪犯上之跡。

translations.literal: With weapons already in use, they truly fell into traces of violating superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Once arms were drawn, they truly walked the path of striking above.

sentences.zh: 敵國起於同舟，況又疏於此者也？

translations.literal: Foes arose from the same boat—how much more when they were estranged like this?
translations.idiomatic: Enemies spring from the same boat—how much more when kinship was thin as this?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：糾糾敬則，臨難不惑。

translations.literal: In praise: Stern and stern Jingze, undaunted in peril.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Upright Jingze, unshaken in the crisis.

sentences.zh: 功成殿寢，誅我蝥賊。

translations.literal: Merit achieved in the hall quarters, cutting down our great foe.
translations.idiomatic: Triumph won within the palace halls, the great pest cut down.

sentences.zh: 顯達孤根，應義南蕃。

translations.literal: Xianda of lonely root, answered righteousness in the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda, rootless and alone, took up the cause in the southern command.

sentences.zh: 威揚寵盛，鼎食高門。

translations.literal: Prestige spread, favor abundant, tripod-fed in high gates.
translations.idiomatic: Glory abroad, favor at flood, tripod-fed in the highest houses.

sentences.zh: 王虧河、兖，陳挫襄、樊。

translations.literal: Wang failed at He and Yan; Chen was checked at Xiang and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang broke on the He and Yan; Chen bent at Xiang and Fan.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
